'''Agility''' is a [[support]] [[Skills|skill]] that allows players to reduce [[stamina]] drain, improve mobility, and navigate [[Ashenfall]] more efficiently through passive world benefits, active traversal mechanics, and skill [[spells]]. At certain levels of this skill, players will be able to increase their carry weight, access shortcuts, and reduce stamina drain on jumping and sprinting.

== Mechanics ==
The skill introduces courses, shortcuts, passives, spells and environmental effects.

===Courses===
[[Agility course]]s are [[activities]] in [[Ashenfall]] where players can train their Agility and receive higher [[experience]] with every level they reach. Players can expect rewards based on each course and their completion time. Each course has a level requirement; the lowest-level course is the [[Chasm Dash]].
{{Map|Agility Course}}

===Shortcuts===
'''[[Kebbit burrows]]''' – Tunnels scattered across the map that players can excavate to open up shortcuts across side routes. Players will be able to dig up kebbit burrows on the map to open up side paths. Failing to navigate these safely at low Agility levels will inflict damage.

''Click on the filter button at the top-right to filter between locations.''
{{Map|Kebbit Burrow (Ghornfell),Kebbit Burrow (Brynmoor),Kebbit Burrow (Dowdun Reach),Kebbit Burrow (Umbral Sands),Kebbit Burrow (Fellhollow)}}

===Passive XP & stamina===
* '''Foot Travel:''' Players will gain 50/200/400 Agility XP at level 1/48/85, passively simply by running on foot across the world. Passive XP generation is strictly disabled while riding mounts.
* '''Stamina Reduction:''' Higher Agility levels will passively reduce the stamina cost of sprinting.

===Environments===
* '''Fall Break:''' Higher levels will automatically trigger a roll when landing from high drops to reduce fall damage. ''Fatal drop heights will still cause death.''
* '''Vault Traps''': Dodging [[Dragonkin vault]]'s traps gives you XP
* '''Dodging''': Dodging enemies attacks gives you XP

=== Spells ===
* '''[[Windstep]]''': Reclassified from Runecrafting to Agility.
** At level 40, landing from Windstep creates an air blast that knocks down nearby enemies.
* '''[[Recall]]''': Leaves a runic marker on the ground; recasting teleports the player back to its location.
** At level 70, if a player suffers a fatal fall while tethered, they are automatically teleported back safely and the tether is consumed.
* '''[[Phase Dash]]''': Allows the use of of a second dash while airborne.

=== Boosts ===
All of the following [[armour]] and [[food]] [[perks]]:
* [[Gyrhawk amulet]] - Provides an additional 100% Agility experience while worn. ''This only applies while exploring the world and consumes [[warped feathers]].''
* [[Gilded gyrhawk amulet]] - Provides an additional 25% Agility experience from [[Agility course]]s, along with the effects of the base amulet.
** The recipe for this item only unlocks if the player has gold record times on all courses, making it locked behind a minimum level of 65 Agility.
* [[Inspiring ring of Agility]] - Provides an additional 5% Agility experience gain while worn.
* [[Knowledgable Nourishment]] - Provides an additional 10% experience gain while active.

One of the following [[potion]] [[perks]]:
* [[Focused Agility]] - Grants a 15% XP Boost while active.
* [[Focused Agility II]] - Grants a 30% XP Boost while active.

'''Animal Magnetism''' is a secondary [[Quests|quest]] in the [[Fractured Plains]]. To start the quest, players must speak to [[Manktongue]], who is located in a ruined house in the south western part of the Fractured Plains.

==Overview==
{{Quest details|desc=Create the Ava's Accumulator|start=Speak to [[Manktongue]] in the southwestern corner of the [[Fractured Plains]].|req=* Decent [[armour]]s and [[weapons]]|item_req=* 1 [[iron bar]]
* 5 [[law rune]]s|rec=* [[Weak antipoison potion]] to travel through the [[Bloodblight Swamp]]|enemies=There are no enemies needed to fight, but the area to gather these items will have:
* [[Putrid rat]]s
* [[Garou]]s
* [[Abyssal demon]]|qtype=secondary}}

==Walkthrough==

===Gathering the ingredients===
To start the quest, speak to Manktongue, who will inform you that he found a [[Advert-Inna-Bottle|message in a bottle]] in the water. Reading it will reveal that it is a message from Ava with the ingredients on how to craft her [[Ava's Accumulator|accumulator]]. Knowing the needed ingredients, you are asked to retrieve each of the following: 1 [[undead chicken]], a [[bundle of undead twigs]], and a [[magnet]], which requires 1 [[iron bar]] and 5 law runes. If you already have the iron and law runes, take them to [[Pulpknuckle]]. He is located in the same cabin upstairs, who will create the magnet for you.

The undead chicken is located within the [[Stormtouched Highlands]], directly north of the quest area. Enter the region, go up the hill, then search for an [[iron ore node]] on the wall. The chicken will be there (map on the bottom right). The Twig is located south of the entrance to [[Bloodblight Swamp]] (map on the bottom right). There is an [[undead tree]]; to get the twig, you will need to interact with it. 
'''''Warning:''' An abyssal demon is known to roam around this area. Be cautious.''
[[File:Map Location.png|alt=In case you cannot locate the Undead Chicken|thumb|Map Location of the Undead Chicken.[[File:Map Location of the Undead Tree..jpg|alt=Map Location of the Undead Tree.|thumb|width=268x268]]Map Location of the Undead Tree.]]

===Finishing up===
After you gather all the ingredients, return to Manktongue, who will create the device for you.

''Congratulations, quest complete!''

==Rewards==
* [[Ava's accumulator]] and the ability to create more.

==Trivia==

* This quest is named after the quest of the {{RSL|Animal Magnetism|same name}}. Just like the quest has almost the same plot, however {{RSL|Ava}} is not present.
** It is explained that she had tossed a message in a bottle out to sea, containing the blueprint of the Ava's accumulator.

'''Attack''' is one of the [[skills]] in ''Runescape: Dragonwilds'' and is one of the three combat styles.  Fighting [[monsters]] using melee combat levels a player's Attack to gain various bonuses that enhance their effectiveness with the skill.

Players can either use their unarmed fists or melee weapons while in combat to earn Attack experience.  The higher the tier of the weapon, the higher the base damage, and thus the more experience earned. To effectively combat, see [[Attack/Strategies]] for more details.

In addition, players can gain experience from [[Skill Tome - Attack|Attack Skill Tomes]] or from special reward tomes like the [[Tome of the Dragon Slayer]].

==Equipment==
===Weapons===
[[Melee weapons]] are split into two categories: one-handed and two-handed weapons. One-handed weapons allow players to also wield a shield.  Some weapons have unique special attacks while some classes of weapons have the same special attack across variants.

=== Shields ===
[[Shields]] allow players to [[parry]] while using melee which can apply [[Perks|debuffs]] to [[monsters]] and reduce the damage received by attacks.

=== Armour ===
Players can earn set bonuses when wearing armour of the same combat type (i.e., melee, ranged, mage) and can mix and match within that type.  For example, a player wearing a [[Paladin's helm]] (melee), [[green dragonhide body]] (ranged), and [[white platelegs]] (melee) will get the second tier of melee set bonuses and the first tier of ranged set bonuses.  The melee armour set bonuses are:
* 1/3 -33% block stamina cost
* 2/3 +50% critical chance after blocking
* 3/3 +25% damage to staggered targets

=== Consumables ===
Players can consume certain crafted materials to receive a temporary boost to damage or allow their melee attacks to apply [[debuffs]] to [[monsters]].

* [[Whetstone]] - provides a percentage buff to melee damage

* [[Weapon barbs]] - applies the [[Bleed]] status effect
* [[Weapon poison]] - applies the [[Poison]] status effect
* [[Fire oil]] - applies the [[Burning]] status effect

== Boosts ==
Players can consume [[potions]], eat [[food]]s, or equip [[trinkets]] to increase Attack experience or increase damage and, indirectly, the experience. 

* [[Lesser Attack potion]] - Increases the chance of landing critical hits with melee by 25% for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Weak Focused Attack potion]] - Provides a 5% XP boost for 5 minutes (300 seconds)
* [[Lesser Focused Attack potion]] - Provides a 5% XP boost for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Sweet veg ball]] - Grants a 10% XP boost for 5 minutes (300 seconds)
* [[Wild pie]] - Grants a 10% XP boost for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Inspiring amulet of Attack]] - Provides a 5% XP boost while worn
* [[Amulet of strength]] - Increases melee damage by 12.5% while worn
* [[Unholy Symbol|Unholy symbol]] - Increases all damage by 15% while lowering maximum HP by 15 points.
* [[Amulet of Glory|Amulet of glory]] - Increases critical damage to all combat style

== Experience Calculation ==
Experience is earned based on the amount of damage dealt to an enemy (except for the [[training dummy]]).  If the attack is normal, players will receive 25% of the damage value as Attack experience.  If the attack is a critical hit, players will instead receive 50% the damage value as Attack experience.

'''Biohazard''' is a secondary [[Quests|quest]] found in [[Dowdun Reach]].

== Overview ==
{{Quest details
|desc = Investigate the strange corruption afflicting the residents of Dowdun Reach.
|item_req =
* 10 [[corrupted essence sample]]s

|rec =
* Arrows or bolts
* Good [[armour]]
|qtype = secondary
|req = Partial completion of [[Black Knight's Fortress (quest)]] for access to [[Dowdun Reach]]
|start = Speak to [[Zanik]] under [[The Approach]], or collect a [[corrupted essence sample]] from [[corrupted raven]]s
|enemies =
* Various monsters within [[Dowdun Reach]]

}}

==Walkthrough==
{{Map|Magical Raven|width=350px|height=350px|center=49918.92,228791.79|zoom=1.5|float=right}}

===Getting started===
You can start this quest in one of two ways: speak to [[Zanik]], who is beneath [[The Approach]], or simply collect a [[corrupted essence sample]] from any [[corrupted raven]] in [[Dowdun Reach]]. Either way, Zanik will ask you to gather 10 corrupted essence samples from corrupted ravens scattered across the region. ''Refer to the map on the right for their locations.''

===The three ingredients===
Once you return to Zanik with all 10 samples, she will ask you to gather three additional items: [[Dragon blood]], [[unholy water]], and a [[twilight lily]].

* Dragon blood: can be obtained by slaying any dragon in Dowdun Reach, or from a [[dragon wolf]] if you want to head back to [[Fellhollow]] and hunt easier enemies.
* Twilight lily: found in [[The Lake]], glowing blue in front of an [[anima tree]]. The Lake is just south-west of Zanik.
* Unholy water: behind [[The Cathedral]], near three [[Zamorakian acolyte]]s, a [[mage of Zamorak]], and two [[elite Black Knight]]s. Look for a statue with water flowing from its hands. ''You do not need to fight any of the enemies here — you can sneak to the fountain south-west of them to collect it.''

===Finding the Source===
Bring all three items back to Zanik. She will ask you to track down the source of the corruption.

Head to [[The Nexus]] and make your way to [[The Grand Hall]]. Use [[windstep]] to climb up to the roof (beware of a [[Black Knight sniper]] and a [[Black Knight guardian]]), and you'll find a corrupted chicken named [[Putrilius]].

Complete the dialogue with Putrilius.

===Returning to Zanik===
Return to Zanik and tell her what you found on the roof of the Grand Hall. She thanks you for your help with investigating the corruption and rewards you for your efforts.

''Quest Completed!''

==Rewards==
* 1x [[Zamorak cape]] (and its recipe)
* 50x [[infernal fragment]]s
** You can collect this by trading 10 corrupted essence samples with Putrilius.

==Transcript==
{{Hastranscript|quest}}

==Trivia==
* This quest is named after one of ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'s'' earliest quests, {{RSL|Biohazard}}.
** Like the original quest, the player will gather samples and try to find a cure.

'''Black dragons,''' also known as '''lesser black dragons,''' are [[power level]] 8 [[Dragon (race)|dragon]]s that can be found in the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid. There are currently only three black dragon spawns.

==Attacks==
* Lunge
* Tail sweep (if behind them)
* Fire Claw Slash
* Poison Blast: The black dragon launches a fire projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
* Fire Breath: The black dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
* Wing Attack: The black dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
* Fly: The black dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
** Fire Breath: The black dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them in to take all of the damage.

Enter Dowdun Reach... | series = Kuldra's Saga }}'''Black Knight's Fortress''' is the seventh primary [[Quests|quest]] and the third in the main storyline of ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''. In this quest, the [[Player Character|Player]] must delve into an ancient mountainous fortress after defeating the revenant dragon [[Imaru]] in order to gain access to the [[Umbral Sands]]. == Quest Overview == {{Quest details|desc=Uncover the secrets of Dowdun Reach in order to unlock your way through to the Umbral Sands.|enemies=* Multiple [[Black Knights]] * Multiple [[mage of Zamorak]] * Multiple [[hellhound]]s * Four (different location) [[shardbound lesser demon]]s * [[Lesser demon]] * [[Blue dragon]] * [[Black Knight Titan]]|item_req=* Steel or Undead Spade * Steel or Mithril Pickaxe * Mithril Logging Axe * Fishing Rod (Any, preferably highest available)|qtype=primary|rec=* Good [[food]], potions * Good armour|req=* [[Withering Heights]] * Level 41 [[Cooking]] to cook [[maple sap]] into [[maple syrup]], or a [[maple toastie]] from a food [[salvage]] spot (1/24)|start=Speak to Death in the Forgotten Temple.}} == Walkthrough == === Part I: The Dark Fortress... === {{Map|Ominous Door|height=250px|width=250px|center=-351.45294,210897.64|float=right}} Speak to [[Death (Grim Reaper)|Death]] in the Forgotten Temple. He will mention about how you did well in Fellhollow, but that there is more for you to do. A colleague of his is waiting for you in the [[Umbral Sands]] to help him, but instructs you to speak to Cathan to gather allies and investigate. You can find Cathan east of Fellhollow, near the ominous gatehouse in the south of [[Silverthorn Keep]]. Speak to Cathan, who greets you, and he will comment about how the adventure never ends. He will then right to it and explain how he has been investigating the ominous gatehouse and, while it leads to some fortress, it is blocking the way to the Umbral Sands. He tells you how he wanted to scout out the place more all spooky-like, but made the mistake of mentioning it to the [[Wise Old Man]]. Knowing how he is like, Cathan mentioned about how he murmured some stuff like "amateur hour wards" and "rubbish defences" before storming down the passageway. Cathan will inform you that, if you want to go after him, to look for him in some sort of central point (like a nexus or something). Go through the open gateway and enter through the '''ominous door''' (Image right). '''Note:''' ''This will play a small intro cutscene to the area''. You will then arrive within [[The Approach]]. Traverse southward through this new region until you enter [[The Courtyard]] where you will meet the Wise Old Man. === Part II: Shadows Within === Speak to the Wise Old Man, who will mention about how you had an easier time getting here than they did and walloping a few troublesome people. He'd then mention about how he was hoping to hunt down another dragon to whittle down Kuldra's forces, but complains about the fortress full of Zamorakians in the way. Despite the bothersome trouble in the way, he mentions how great it is that you're here to help get them moving again. Troubling thing is, he mentions how the way is blocked by someone called "the gatekeeper" and he isn't sure who or what it may be. Despite not being aware of who or what it is, the Wise Old Man tells you that [[Doric]] is currently working on dispelling a nasty magical barrier further ahead in the Nexus. He then says how it might be a good idea to make a base camp here first. After making a base camp, follow the path leading up into the fortress. Arrive at [[The Nexus]] and speak to Doric. Once you speak to him, he will mention about how crazed the Black Knights are along with how they look like they should have all died long ago. He mentions how the problem is that you are all stuck here and he has everything to get the door open. As far as Doric can tell, everything seems to be connected to a [[Avisk|great big stone]] next to him. He says that it looks broken and, theorising a way to get past the door, might need to fix it using some missing pieces. Inspect the stone. This will reveal a small dialogue from the stone itself describing how it is broken, shards of itself are missing, and that you should find the missing pieces to repair it. It will then give you authorisation to look around the keep and to access the [[Nodestone|Nexus nodes]] scattered around [[Dowdun Reach]]. === Part III: Shard Hunting === '''Item(s) needed:''' ''Spade, Pickaxe, Logging Axe.''[[File:Shard Map Locations.png|thumb|width=405x405|The locations for the Shards of Dreaming Stone]] [[File:Underground Entrance.png|thumb|Follow arrow past all the Hellrat pens and turn left. Follow the staircase down to the lowest level. Explore this underground region for the three Shards of the Dreaming Stone.]] [[File:Underground Entrance2.png|thumb|Second entrance to underground region.]] After inspecting the Dreaming Stone, you will discover that there are thirteen [[Shard of the Dreaming Stone|shards]] (marked on your map with yellow circles) that are needed to repair it. These shards are scattered throughout Dowdun Reach and require you to either interact with characters, scenery objects, or solve puzzles to acquire them. While most are above-ground, there are three that are kept underground. Once you have collected all thirteen shards, head back to the Dreaming Stone. ====[[The Cathedral]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |South-West |Cut down vines w/ mithril logging axe then standard interact |You can acquire the cathedral shard by heading south-west to a courtyard full of Zamorakian acolytes and mages and, using your mithril (or above) logging axe, cut down the vines. As the mages and acolytes are hostile by default, you will need to take them down first. |} ====[[The Garrison]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |East |Defeat [[Sergeant Blister]] |He is located underground in The Garrison region, protected by two hellhounds and a small host of skeletons. The requirements to interact/collect this shard are the same as defeating the shardbound lesser demons. |- |West |Standard interact |Navigate past the elite Black Knight and two Zamorakian acolytes to an open wall with some wooden boards. Use the [[Windstep]] spell to jump up and across to the nearby adjacent tower. Once you have arrived, either defeat or avoid the elite Black Knight to interact with the shard. |} ====[[The Grand Hall]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |East |Interact with [[Spittletoe]] |Spittletoe instructs you to collect five Maple Sap. The second lever is inside of a cave nearby protected by a thorny vine wall along the rock wall to the right of the shard. You will need a mithril or better logging axe to chop these vines. The third and final lever is on the top level of the nearby stone ruins, located beside the air anima vent. You'll need to use [[Windstep]] to reach this level. This area is guarded by a lesser blue dragon. |- |South-East |Standard interact |Follow along the lower area cliffs to reach an area where you can jump across. You'll also locate a group of hellhounds on your way there, but you can either ignore them or defeat them until you locate a series of beams. Traverse the beams by jumping up to the next level until you reach the top where you'll need to jump across to the stone rock where the shard is located. '''Note:''' You'll need plenty of air runes to use Windstep for this particular jumping puzzle. An alternative way is to equip your [[leggings of lightness]] and use Windstep from where you received the previous shard from finding the three levers, down to the cliffs. Be sure '''not''' to jump and head down, instead, fall with the spell and the leggings to avoid damage. |} ====[[The Pastures]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |North |Mine a [[granite deposit]] |Reach the highest part of the goblin-infested fortress. In the middle of the area, there is a granite deposit that hides the shard. You can either avoid or defeat the blue dragon here to get to the shard, but you can use the [[Rocksplosion]] spell to quickly interact with the shard. |- |East |Interact button |Defeat the goblins in the immediate area of the shard before interacting with it. |} ====Underground Shards==== These are located underground, they can be completed in any order. =====[[The Crypt]] (underground)===== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |The Crypt |Dig with spade/shovel |Navigate to The Crypt in the underground region. Before searching for the shard, defeat the zogre here. This will save you trouble later. Interact with the [[Hastily Scrawled Note|note]] next to the goblin corpse to learn that the shard is buried in a grave. Dig at ''any'' of the graves until you uncover the shard. '''Note:''' ''The location of this shard is randomized for every world''. |} =====[[The Demon Gate]] (underground)===== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |The demon gate |Defeat 2x [[shardbound lesser demon]] |Navigate to the lowest part of the region. There is a lever-activated elevator that will take you down to the demon gate region. For easier traversal later, interact with the nearby nodestone to connect it to the Nexus. Navigate through the pathways until you reach the stone structure and defeat the two lesser demons guarding the shard. |} =====[[The Lake]] (underground)===== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |The Lake |Speak with [[Offalfoot]] |He will ask you to give him one of the fish nearby (requires an empty inventory slot), so you'll need to grab one from the nearby pool of fish. This will give you an [[unusual trout]] and give this trout to Offalfoot. He'll give you the shard. '''Note:''' You do need a fishing rod (the highest level is recommended) and this can be done with level 1 Fishing. You will encounter [[Delrom]] when traversing to through this location. |} === Part IV: Remember the Titans === Interact with the Dreaming Stone. It will say that it is restored, but it will reveal that it was evil! It will claim that its name will rattle in your tiny skull like the echoes within a cave. The Dreaming Stone then reveals its name to be '''Avisk the eternal''' whose mind had ever graced the Aughra, but as it tries to enslave you and become its thrall, it seemed stunned. This will reveal two dialogue options (both of which are about destroying the stone), but choose option one. This will force the crystal to acknowledge your logic and, in its own way, apologise for being overzealous and how it happens when you've been alone in the psyche of Black Knights for too long. It then blames the Cthonian before taking down the barrier. It then warns you to be wary of Lord Rasmodel (aka the [[Black Knight Titan]]) as it had a bit of a mishap when he smashed the Dreaming Stone to pieces. Now, he's got some of the Dreaming Stone , some of a demon, and a whole lot of anger issues. End the dialogue and the Dreaming Stone will be fully repaired. Interact with the newly-dropped Barrier and you'll arrive in [[The Bastion]]. Head up all the stairs (be mindful of some gaps which can be Windstepped) until you reach the top. He also pleads for you to be patient - and to stay your hammer - as he will help get you into the desert soon. He then gives you a reward (read: bribe) for not smashing him to pieces with your hammer. '''Congratulations! Quest Complete!''' == Rewards == * 1x [[Black Knight's Fortress reward pack]] ** 1x [[Tome of the Titan]] *** +750 XP to Magic, Ranged, and Attack ** 1x [[Titan's wrath]] *Recipe to creating the [[Titan's wrath]] 2h sword ==Transcript== {{Hastranscript|quest}} == Required to Complete == ''This quest is required to complete the following:'' * [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]] == Trivia == * The quest's name is inspired by ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'s'' and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}'s'' variant of the quest. ** In ''RuneScape'' the quest was replaced by {{RSL|The Death of Chivalry}} on 13 August 2013. *It is the third quest in the game's Early Access, also known as Kuldra's Saga. {{Black Knight's Fortress}} {{Quests}}

'''Milliburn Rasmodel''', also known as '''Lord Rasmodel''', and the '''Black Knight Titan''' is a [[power level]] 6 [[boss]] [[Monsters|monster]], released with [[Dowdun Reach]]. He is the old commander of the [[Black Knights]] within Dowdun Reach, who was resurrected by the [[Avisk|Dreaming Stone]], and guards the passageway to the [[Umbral Sands]].

==Drops==
{{DropsTableHead}}
{{DropsLine|name=Broken Titan's Wrath|quantity=1|rarity=Always}}
{{DropsLine|name=Ascension Shard (Power Level 6)|quantity=20-30|rarity=Always}}
{{DropsTableBottom}}

==History==
Milliburn was the eldest son of the Rasmodels' house, a noble house from the mainland, who worshipped [[Saradomin]] before rebelling against him. When the [[Children of Shadows]] became allied with the family, Milliburn's brother would play pranks on the members who became bodyguards to the nobles. When his father died, he became the head of the house. During his rule, he kept having dreams and visions, which eventually led him to believe that he needed to form the Shadow Knights, believing [[Imaru]], [[Xikotal]], and [[Fellhollow]] itself could not be trusted. 

After reforming the Children of Shadows into the '''Black Knights''', Milliburn would continue to rule over Dowdun Reach. After the [[Dragon Rebellion]], when Kuldra ordered her dragons to lay waste to the inhabitants of [[Ashenfall]], the Black Knights were able to hold their own against the dragon attacks. Their defences were greatly strengthened thanks to the '''Dreaming Stone''', but it would sow whisper and madness in his and others' minds. After a period of time with the stone, which had caused distrust, Milliburn had decided to destroy it, finally being free of the madness. Before he could do anything else, his family, the Rasmodel house, would appear before him, telling him to rest, that they would take it from here. Now his body remains within the [[Black Knight's Fortress]], controlled by his insanity and unknowingly guarding the way to [[Umbral Sands]].

==Journal==
{{journal entry|The Dreaming Stone had been shattered.

Lord Rasmodel, on his knees, heard no voices. For the first time in too, too long, he could hear his own breath. His heart played a welcome beat. For decades, he had felt like he floated above the world. Now he was part of it again.

Footsteps. Lord Rasmodel lifted his head wearily. Who would interrupt this moment?

Tinging around him was his family. The Rasmodels. They were all there - all the ones he knew, and loved and had met. They were dressed as the finest nobility, the Rasmodels at their height. They had regained their standing - the name meant something again.

His father knelt down and lifted Lord Rasmodel's bloody chin. Their eyes met. " Rest," his father said. "We will take it from here."

Milliburn Rasmodel, twenty-fifth Lord of Rasmodel, took his retirement.
}}

}}'''Brink of Extinction''' is a secondary [[Quests|quest]] within the [[Umbral Sands]]. Players must speak with [[KotHaar-Hok-Zi]] in order to start the quest.

== Overview ==
{{Quest details|qtype=secondary|start=Speak to the Kot-Haar Zi in The Burning Spire|rec=None|enemies = KotHaar-Hok-Zi|req=Partial completion of [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]]
| item_req =
* 3 [[raw beltfish]]
* [[Cactus steak]]
|desc=Help Zi to become a real KotHaar}}
== Walkthrough ==
=== Getting Started ===
Speak to Zi in Umbral Sands to start this quest. KotHaar-Zi is located in The Burning Spire, directly south-east of Sinking Pyramid on an 'L-shaped' island.
===Protection from Scorch===
KotHaar-Zi will inform you that their body was not made to survive Scorch and asks for assistance with adapting. They ask you to bring them 3 [[raw beltfish]] and 1 [[cactus steak]].

==="THE GAUNTLET OF FIRE!"===
After returning to KotHaar-Zi, they will tell you about four pedestals, scattered around the Burning Spire area - giant black blocks with fire on top. They ask you to touch all four of them in any order and then return to KotHarr-Zi. A blue circle will be added to your map, showing the area the four pedestals are located at. 

* Pillar 1: Located east of the Sunken Pyramid, on top of a large rock structure.
* Pillar 2: Located north of the Sunken Pyramid, behind KotHaar-Zi. 
* Pillar 3: Located west of the Sunken Pyramid.
* Pillar 4: Located south of the Sunken Pyramid, south-west from KotHaar-Zi. 

After interacting with all four pillars, return to KotHaar-Zi.

===Cave of Screams===

After talking to KotHaar-Zi, they will tell you they are heading to the [[Cave of Screams]], which is located west of the Sunken Pyramid. At the entrance to the Cave of Screams, there will be a bouncer who will ask for a password.

Make your way to the Cave of Screams entrance, located in the top-left corner of The Burning Spire, directly right of the tree icon found on the map.

Talk to the [[KotHaar Bouncer]]. Pick any of the three dialogue options - it doesn't matter which you choose. After picking the third dialogue option, you will be given a [[KotHaar numbering for dummies]] scroll. Inspect the scroll in your quest inventory. 

Talk to the Bouncer again and select the option which says "Two triangles separated by a line?".

You will now be able to access the Cave of Screams. The bouncer will warn you that KotHaar-Zi has changed, and that their core must be forged into a new body, a new body which is controlled by [[Fuzan]].

===Reforged Zi===
Upon entering the Cave of Screams, you'll immediately be met by two hostile [[KotHaar-Xil]] and a hostile [[KotHaar-Hok-Zi|Reforged Zi]]. Defeat all three enemies. After Reforged Zi is defeated, [[Zi core]] will appear on the ground - grab it and then exit the cave.

===Return to the Bouncer===

Talk to the Bouncer. They will award you for assisting with Zi and reward you with the [[plate of pure obsidian]], which unlocks recipe for [[obsidian cape]].

''Quest Completed!''

== Rewards ==

* 1x [[plate of pure obsidian]]

Combat:
{{external|os|rs|rsc}}
{{otheruses|def=no|the music played during combat|Combat (music)}}
'''Combat''' is an event in ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' in which two or more players and/or creatures fight. Combat is based around a randomly generated numbers in the form of "damage", which deplete a target's life points. The damage done by the parties involved is determined by several factors, including weapons and equipment.

Players can influence their effectiveness in combat in many ways, such as boosting their combat via [[perks]].

== Combat ==
The three combat classes in ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' are '''melee''', '''ranged''', and '''magic.'''

=== Melee ===
* [[Armour#Melee Armour|Melee armour]] offers a -% in block stamina cost, +% in crit chance after blocking, and a +% on damage to staggered opponents on all three sets.
** Melee armour also has a greater defence against melee attacks, while having the weakest defence against magic attacks.
* Melee weapons have 3 damage types: '''slash''', '''stab''', and '''crush'''.

=== Ranged ===
* [[Armour#Ranged Armour|Ranged armour]] offer a +% stealth speed, -% in ranged attack stamina cost, and a +% to weak point damage on all three sets.
** Ranged armour also has greater defence against range attacks, while having a equal defence stats in magic and melee.
* Ranged weapons has one damage type: '''ranged'''.

=== Magic ===
* [[Armour#Magic Armour|Magic armour]] offers a -% stamina regen delay, +% magic attack speed, and +% in magical crit change.
** Magic armour also has a greater defence against magic attack, while having the weakest defence against melee attacks.
* There are three spell damage types: '''air''', '''fire''', and '''water'''.

=== Combat variables ===
There are several variables in combat that moderate an entity's performance. Life points are possessed by players and foes, whereas the other mechanisms are used in foes sparingly or restrictively.

* [[File:Health Icon.png|frameless|width=29x29]] [[health]] -  Health represent how much damage a player or creature can withstand. When an entity loses all its life points, it dies. A player's maximum life points is at 100. The primary method of recovering life points is either staying outside of combat for regen, or eating [[food]]. Armour also provides reduction to how much damage you can receive.
** [[File:Sangine Urn Map Icon (un-used).png|frameless|width=35x35]] [[sanguine urn]] - Sanguine urns are items found within Ashenfall that boosts max health by 10. Collecting them all would provide 310 total health.
* [[File:Stamina Icon.png|frameless|width=29x29]] [[stamina]] - Stamina represents how much energy a player has to be able to attack, dodge or block. If a player runs out of stamina, they will be unable to attack or dodge and blocking will cause them to stagger ([[parry]]ing can regain some stamina). The Primary method of recovering stamina is allowing it to regen on its own. There are perks that grants some reduction to stamina.
* [[File:Special Attack icon.png|frameless|width=35x35]][[Special Action|special action]] - Special action represent how much power a player has and can use. Certain weapons allow players to do special actions, where it would cost 25, 33, or even 50% of their special action energy.

=== Combat stats ===
Combat stats are levels that determines a player's benefit when fighting in one of the three combat styles. In ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''',''''' players have three of the following combat style and benefits:

* [[File:Attack.png|frameless|width=40x40]] [[Attack]] - Per level, it decreases the cost of stamina when using melee weapons, and grants benefits at certain levels:
** At level 5 you unlock the ability to parry. 
** At level 8 you unlock the ability to use use weapon [[special action]]s. 
** At level 11 you unlock the spell [[Tempest Shield]]. 
** At level 16 you unlock the spell [[Weapon Expertise]].
** At level 20 you unlock the spell [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]].
** At level 23 you unlock the ability [[Adaptability]].
** At level 30 you unlock the spell [[Enchant Weapon: Air]].
** At level 30 you unlock the item [[whetstone|whetstone.]]
** At level 50 you unlock the spell [[Enchant Weapon: Water]].
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Attack cape]].
* [[File:Ranged.png|frameless|width=36x36]][[Ranged]] - Per level, it increases the chances of retrieving your arrows or bolts from enemies' loot when they die and grants benefits at certain levels:
** At level 3 you unlock the ability [[Quick Action]].
** At level 8 you unlock the ability [[Trick Shot]].
** At level 12 you unlock the spell [[Snare]].
** At level 15 you unlock [[weapon poison]] (called Toxic Behaviour in-game).
** At level 18 you unlock [[Hunter's Sense]].
** At level 22 you unlock [[weapon barbs]] (called Make 'Em Bleed in-game).
** At level 25 you unlock the spell [[Spectral Arrows]].
** At level 30 you unlock the ability [[Crossbow Trick Shot]].
** At level 35 you unlock the ability to create [[enchanted crossbow bolts]].
** At level 40 you unlock the [[Venomous Trapper]] effect of Snare.
** At level 45 you unlock [[fire oil]] to create [[fire arrow]]s
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Ranged cape]].
* [[File:Magic.png|frameless|width=37x37]][[Magic]] - Per level, it decreases the cost of stamina when attacking with magic and grants benefits at certain levels:
** At level 5 you unlock the ability [[Secondary Attacks]].
** At level 7 you unlock the ability to cast [[Water Magic|Water magic]].
** At level 11 you unlock the spell [[Surge]].
** At level 16 you unlock the ability [[Arcane Expertise]]
** At level 20 you unlock the perk [[Runic Refund]]
** At level 21 you unlock the ability to cast [[Fire Magic|Fire magic]].
** At level 25 you unlock the perk [[Afterimage]] from the Surge spell.
** At level 30 you unlock the spell [[Confuse]]
** at level 39 you unlock the item [[magical focus]].
** At level 44 you unlock the perk [[Greater Confuse]] from the Confuse spell.
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Magic cape]].
* [[File:Artisan.png|frameless|width=34x34]][[Artisan]] - Per level, it decreases the durability loss on [[equipment]], that includes weapons and armour.
** At level 56 you unlock the spell [[Magical Mending]].
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Artisan cape]].

==== Stamina reduction ====
Within ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' there are method of reducing stamina when using combat from devouring [[Food|food or drinks]] that provide additional perks, such as [[Infusions]]. Infusions can be created by using the [[Cooking]] skill, and provides benefits such as stamina reduction when using one of the three combat style.

=== Combat Equipment ===
In ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'', combat equipment, such as [[armour]]s and [[weapons]] provide additional stats boosts to help you either do more damage, or reduce the damage you will receive. Using good equipment is essential to combat, as well as dodging and parrying.

==== Weapons ====
{{Main|Weapons}}
Weapons are items held that uses the either one or both hands to use and contributes on the player's base damage, damage multiplier and/or attack speed. Each weapon have a different [[power level]] that determines their stats. The higher the power level the greater the stats is. Some weapons, like bows and crossbows have their own base damage, which is increased when using ammunition, which adds a damage multiplier. 

Certain weapons, like [[black sword]] or the [[zombie axe]] have special effects that does better damage against certain [[Monsters|enemies]].

==== Armour ====
{{Main|Armour}}
Armours are items worn by the players that increases their defence against certain attack style, reducing incoming damage while providing buffs as well.. They also have a set effect which requires all three of the same combat style to unlock all three effect. Each armour have different power level that determines their stats. The higher the power level the greater the defence is.

==== Trinkets ====
{{Main|Trinkets}}
Trinkets are items worn by the players that grants additional effects to the wearer, such as the [[ring of recoil]], which deflects certain percentage of damages back to the attacker(s), or the [[salve amulet]], which increases damage to undead enemies. The [[ring of life]] provides a teleport back to your [[bed]] when your HP is reduces to 1.

=== Special Action ===
{{Main|Special Action}}
Most, if not all weapons have the ability to use a special action, this is an ability that allows the player to use the max damage of their attack, at the cost of their Special Action Bar. Some like the [[abyssal whip]] or the [[crystal bow]] allows a special attack that provides extra damage with other effects, like staggering or extra damages. A good numbers of weapons have special actions, they are

* [[Swords]]
* [[Greatswords]]
* [[Daggers]]
* [[Greataxes]]
* [[Warhammer]]
* [[Maces]]
* [[Scimitar]]
* [[Staves]]

=== Damage ===
{{Main|Hitsplat}}
There are different type of weapon damages, including buffs, they are:
* Stab
* Slash
* Crush
* Ranged
* Fire
* Water
* Earth {{Sic|Unreleased Damage type.}}
* [[Burning]]
* [[Bleed]]
* [[Poison]]
* Immunity
There are also [[Critical Strike|critical damage]], resistance damage and weak to damage, which both indicates when a target is receiving critical damage, is resistance to a damage type, or is weak to the damage type. 

====Weak spots====
{{Main|Ranged#Weak spots}}
Some enemies have spots around them that usually allow players to deal critical damage; these are called weak spots. Note that there is no cooldown for critical damage when targeting the monsters' weak spots.

A means to explain how a melee user beats a ranged user, a ranged user beats a magic user, and a magic user beats a melee user. In ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds,'' there is no system. ==Walkthrough==
===Collecting the ingredients===
To start the quest, speak to Slopfinger, located in the south-west area of the Fractured Plains, near the border of the [[Stormtouched Highlands]]. Speaking to him, you learn that he is trying to make a cake, but his assistant, [[Manktongue]], is ignoring him, so he asks you to assist him in showing that he can prove his worth as a chef. He'll ask you to collect 4 [[egg]]s, 6 [[wheat]]s and 1 [[bucket of milk]]. The bucket of milk is the easiest ingredient; there is a [[cow]] just outside of the building within a pen. Interact with it and go through all the options, '''BUT''' do not milk it, as it will willingly give you milk.

For the rest of the ingredients, it is advised that you build a lodestone at the quest area so you can head over to [[Bramblemead Valley]] or [[Temple Woods]] to collect some eggs from [[chicken]]<nowiki/>s. Alternatively, you can chop down trees and get a [[bird nest]]. Killing goblins is required to collect [[wheat seeds]], or looking through [[chest]]s.

Once you collect all the ingredients, return to Slopfinger, and he will have you bake the cake for him. After baking the cake, speak to him again, and he will ask that you speak to Manktongue and show him the cake. Speak to Slopfinger one last time to complete the quest.

{{External|rs=Critical strike}}
'''Critical strikes''' deal an additional 25% increased damage from base damage roll (125% base damage).

==Mechanics==
The player’s critical hit chance affects the rate at which each attack can critically hit, dealing 25% more critical hit damage (x1.25). The base critical hit chance is 10%, and this rate (not damage) can be improved through [[perks]].

To calculate the damage multiplier of an attack or event, the following formula is used:

* For example: <math>(( 1 - 0.10) \times 1.00) + (0.10 \times 1.25)</math> indicates a 10% critical strike chance, no base damage boosts, and all critical strikes deal 125% damage. In this example (the baseline for all players), the equation would equal 1.025, meaning on average (true statistical average over many events) each attack deals 1.025x more damage per swing than displayed in the chart below due to critical strikes and base damage boosts.
The [[amulet of accuracy]] can increase the critical strike damage of [[Ranged]] attacks by 15%.

{{external|rs|os|rsc}}
'''Currencies''' are items that can be exchanged and are used for various transactions in ''[[RuneScape: Dragonwilds]]''. There is no main form of currency in the game, as only five known shops take different currencies. 

== In-game currencies ==
There are currently three types of currencies used in-game: 
* [[Soul fragment]]s, which can be collected within [[Fellhollow]] by killing [[undead]] or completing [[quests]] within the region and can be used in [[Death (Grim Reaper)#Death's Exchange|Death's Exchange]].
* [[Infernal fragment]]s, which can be collected within [[Dowdun Reach]] by killing [[Black Knights]], [[demon]]s or completing quests within the region, and can be used in [[Postie Pete#Evil Emporium|Evil Emporium]].
* [[Garou chit]]s, which can be collected throughout [[Umbral Sands]] and used to trade with merchants.

==Walkthrough==
{{Map|Dog Days|width=350px|height=350px|center=83000,0|zoom=2|float=right}}
===Investigate the Garou and their rituals===
Talk to Vannaka, who is standing under a cliff in the eastern part of the Highlands (see the image). He will tell you about the garou and ask you to investigate their rituals.

Go to the location of the lore book, beneath the wyrm corpse, and read it. It is advised to go around and approach from the north, as there are fewer enemies. There is a [[garou thane]] next to the book, but facing the opposite direction, so you can sneak there and read the book.

===Challenging the King===
After you read the book, you have to defeat the [[Garou King]] and get his [[Tainted King's Token|tainted token]]. Go to the castle in the north-west of the Highlands. Use [[Windstep]] as much as you can, to avoid as many enemies as you can.
At the top of the hill, in the castle, you need to defeat the king, who is a thane, and his attacks are the same. It is suggested to cast Windstep onto the arches of the Garou King's ruined temple to safespot its attacks.

===Ritual of Purification===
Go back to Vannaka after you get the token. He will tell you that the token is tainted and needs to be purified. Head north to the location of [[Lougrim's Shrine]], kill the [[garou druid]]s there, and use it. The shrine will tell you that for the ritual, you need 2 [[ram horn]]s and 3 [[Shocking Plant Bulb|Shock Bulbs]], so kill [[ram]]s and [[wild lapulis vine]]s until you have enough materials. Then, go back to the shrine and perform the ritual of purification to receive a [[Purified King's Token|purified token]].

Go back to Vannaka and talk with him.

''Congratulations, Quest complete!''

==Rewards==
* [[Garou highborn's cloak]]

==Walkthrough==
{{Map|Dragon Slayer|float=right|center=136814,73201}}
===Part I: To Slay Dragons!===
To start this quest, speak to the [[Wise Old Man]] in [[Bramblemead Valley|Bramblemead Village]] and he will instruct you on getting started with hunting down [[General Velgar]]. Before you can start hunting dragons, you need a shelter. He will tell you to build a little shelter, with at least a [[bed roll]] in it, which you have to claim. To be able to claim it, you need to build at least a foundation, 3 walls, and a ceiling, and place the bed roll in it. Once you finish your task, talk with him again.

He will tell you that one of the adventurers, young [[Cathan]] is missing and needs to be found. To do this, he will cast a locator spell, but he needs some [[antlers]] for that. Hunt down [[deer]]s in the valley and bring the antlers to him. As they tend to run away, you need a [[ranged]] or [[magic]] weapon to kill them.

The spell will point you to a nearby castle within the valley, so this will be your next destination.

===Part II: A Lost Adventurer...===
When you arrive at the [[Keep of Blue Flames]], it will look eerily similar to Lumbridge Castle, but with Bandosian banners flying. This place will have a ''lot'' of goblins, so pack some [[food]]. You will find Cathan's Journal lying at the top of the castle next to a loot chest. Read his journal and you will learn that you need to go to the [[Whispering Swamp]] to locate a "blue-flame door". At this point, [[Velgar]] will descend to the keep, spraying poison next to the gate, then attack with his poison puddles. You can either wait for his attack to end or just run out of the keep, dodging the strikes.

Journey through the "blue-flame door" (the [[dragonkin vault]] [[Vertentis Kara]]) and speak to Spitfoot at the end of the vault. He will detail Cathan's journey, his betrayal, and his desire to go to [[Ghornfell]]. Take this information back to the [[Wise Old Man]] in the Bramblemead Valley, and he will remark about Cathan's foolish recklessness. After telling you that if he is willing to brave the [[Garou (race)|Garou]], Cathan must have a way to deal with Velgar, he will ask you to dive into [[Ghornfell]] to pick up his trail.

Once you arrive in the [[Fractured Plains]] (an area of Ghornfell), you will then be prompted to go check out [[Velgar's Rise]], a monumental tower at the heart of the region, for any information on Cathan's whereabouts.

===Part III: The Beginnings of a Legend...===
When you arrive at the Rise, you will encounter [[Cathan]]'s ghost. Speak to him and he will talk about how he was so sure he could defeat Velgar (after remarking how death sucked). He will tell you that the [[Garou (race)|Garou]] mobbed him and dragged him to the tower, holding him down in front of Velgar as they sacrificed him. He will then give you a recipe to make a [[challenge horn]] that can challenge Velgar in his tower.

You need to travel to both [[Bloodblight Swamp]] and [[Stormtouched Highlands]] to gather the materials for the horn.
* In the Highlands you have to travel past the skeleton which the [[Garou (race)|Garou]] use as home on the western part and you can find a dragon skull. You can mine it's [[Dragon's Tooth|teeth]] with an [[iron pickaxe]] to get the [[dragon tooth]].
* In the swamp, you have to travel to the castle on the most southern point. In the castle you can find the [[bloodwood tree]] (and some [[Garou (race)|Garou]]), and you can harvest it with [[iron logging axe]] to gather the [[bloodwood sap]].
Combine them with 5 [[bronze bar]] and you can create the horn.

===Part IV: Fight for your life===
When you have the horn, grab your best armour and weapon, bring some [[antipoison]] potions and [[food]], and enter [[Velgar's Rise]]. The top of the tower is basically a triangle, with a pedestal at the centre. When you place the horn on the [[dragonkin altar]], Velgar will arrive on one corner.

He will use poison spray and poison puddle bombs or stomp both his legs, which will create spikes in your direction. If you get close to using melee, he will stomp one leg, which is closer to you, and also bite forward and hit sideways with his head. All of his attacks are delayed, so you can prepare and dodge, and between each attack he will wait a bit.

After he loses 1/4 of his health, he will fly away and use his poison puddle bomb attack multiple times. After that, he will land on another corner, the next of the previous one, clockwise. In the second phase, he will use multiple attacks one after another, before he waits a bit. The attacks are the same as in the previous phase.

After his health is brought to half, he will again fly away, and his signature attack will happen again. He will land again on another edge, still next to the previous one, clockwise, and the fight continues like before. He will once more fly away when he loses 3/4 of his health. He will land on the original edge, where he can be attacked again.

Once Velgar is defeated, you will get his [[Velgar's Head|head]]. Go outside of the tower, speak to the [[Wise Old Man]] (who has replaced Cathan's ghost), and give him the head to complete this quest.

'''Congratulations! Quest complete!'''

==Rewards==

** After following Cathan into Ghornfell - containing 3 [[clay]], 3 [[redberries]], and 3 [[harralander]].
** End of quest - containing a [[Tome of the Dragon Slayer]], a [[noxious draconic visage]], and an [[anti-dragon shield]].

'''Farming''' is one of the [[skills]] in ''Runescape: Dragonwilds'' and allows players to grow various plants.  The skill was released as part of the 0.10 [[Fellhollow]] update.

To level up this skill, players must weed, sow, fertilize, water, cure, and harvest crops.

To begin, players must complete [[Growing Pains]] by talking to the [[Wise Old Man]] in [[Bramblemead Valley]].  Once the [[Quests|quest]] is completed, players can create [[farming plot]]s to get started with Farming.

==Items==
===Seeds===
[[Seeds]] can be collected from picking wild plants, looting [[chest]]s and [[pack]]s, or harvesting grown plants. Players can then equip [[seeds]] and, when used, will sow plants in [[farming plot]]s or the ground. Planting trees requires [[tree farming]] unlocked at level 20.

[[Redberry bush]]es, [[dwellberry bush]]es, [[cadavaberry bush]]es, [[ash tree]]s, [[oak tree]]s, and [[willow tree]]s can be harvested without having to replant seeds.

==Mechanics==
===Growth cycles===
Seeds take 2 in-game days to grow (progressing at the beginning of each day) and have several growth stages with distinct visual graphics. While growing, plants can become diseased. Diseased crops cannot be harvested, and if left untreated, will die the following day. Planting seeds in a plot for their region, watering, and composting them will significantly lower (but not remove) the chance of disease. Healthy and harvestable crops no longer have a chance to become diseased, and can be left when no longer farming.

Each plant has a base DiseaseChance:
* 0.3: [[Potato]], [[tomato]], and [[pumpkin]]
* 0.4: [[Cabbage]], [[flax]], [[harralander]], [[marrentil]], [[dwellberry]], [[onion]], [[kwuarm]], [[swamp weed]], [[snapdragon]], [[toadflax]], [[watermelon]], and [[avantoe]]
* 0.5: [[Redberry]] and [[irit]]
* 0.6: [[Wheat]] and [[cadavaberry]]
* 0.75: [[Corpse cotton]], [[desert weed]], [[bunny cactus]], [[barrel cactus]], and [[fibrous pipe cactus]]

Or in other words, a [[potato]] has a base 30% chance of becoming diseased each growth cycle.

===Weeding===
When [[farming plot]]s are first placed, they have a layer of weeds. As long as nothing is planted in the plot, layers of weeds will continue to build up once each day, up to 3 layers per plot. These will need to be removed with a shovel before anything can be planted. Each layer will provide a base 3 XP and 3 [[weeds]]. Higher power level shovels can do so in fewer actions.

===Seeding===
Players must equip [[seeds]] to then use them, which will seed [[farming plot]]s or the ground, depending on the seed used. This provides a base 5 XP per seed planted, regardless of type or plot.

===Watering===
Farming plots can be watered once per day, which will significantly lower the chance of disease and slightly increase yield. Players can use [[watering cans]] on natural water sources (e.g., ponds and rivers) to fill the can with [[dirty water]] or collect [[clean water]] from [[rain catcher]]s or [[well]]s and then use the can directly on the plots. Alternatively, players can cast [[Humidify]] with their watering can in their inventory, which will use whichever water is inside to water the plots in a straight line in front of the player. Note, however, that the items with the same name gathered by hand and then cooked at a [[campfire]] or [[grill]] cannot be used to fill a [[watering can]]. 

Crops have their own individual chance of disease, which are further modified by whether they are watered and with what type:
* No water - Unwatered crops have a further 0.8x chance of disease
* [[Dirty water]] - Offers a lower 0.3x chance of disease and 1.15x yield
* [[Clean water]] - Offers an even lower 0.2x chance of disease and 1.15x yield

Watering a plot with a plant that was just seeded, is harvestable, diseased, or dead will provide a small base 2 XP, however watering growing plants in an [[ash farming plot]] provides base 15 XP, an [[oak farming plot]] provides base 30 XP, a [[willow farming plot]] provides base 45 XP, and a [[yew farming plot]] provides base 60 XP.

Rain will automatically water plots with [[clean water]], which can save time, however it will not provide XP or cure disease.

===Fertilising===
Fertilising plots helps prevent disease and increase yield. A plot only needs to be fertilized once during its cycle until it is fully harvested and cleared. Players can convert organic materials into [[compost]] at a [[compost bin]] or [[super compost]] at a [[super compost bin]], and then collect and spread the fertiliser with a [[compost bucket]] on plots. 

As there are not currently any higher power level [[compost bucket]]s, it is recommended to craft and carry several at once to minimise how frequently you need to return to the [[compost bin]]s while composting [[farming plot]]s. [[Compost]] provides a base 10 XP per plot, while [[super compost]] provides a base 50 XP.

* [[Compost]] - Offers 0.5x disease chance and 1.5x yield increase.
* [[Super compost]] - Offers 0.25x disease chance and 1.75x yield increase.

===Curing===
Diseased plants will change graphically with a brownish-yellow haze, and read "Diseased" when hovering over the plot. Players must cure the plant to prevent it from dying if left diseased for too long. There are three ways of cleansing diseased plants:

* [[Plant cure]]
* [[Humidify]] with the [[Cleansing Rain]] passive unlocked after level 50
* [[Farming cape]]'s special effect acts as an infinite source of [[plant cure]]s

If the plant is cleansed, it will return to its current growth stage. This means that if a plant is diseased in its final growth stage but the player cures it the same day, the player can harvest it without waiting another day. Curing a plant provides a base 3 XP.

===Harvesting===
The yield when harvesting can be modeled as so:

<code>Yield = ceil( ceil( ceil(BaseYield * SecateursYieldMultiplier) * CompostYieldMultiplier) * WaterYieldMultiplier)}}</code>
* '''BaseYield''' = 3 for [[flax]], [[corpse cotton]], [[desert weed]], [[bunny cactus]], [[barrel cactus]], and [[fibrous pipe cactus]], and 5 for every other seed.
* '''SecateursYieldMultiplier''' = 1.25. The [[iron secateurs]] do not work with [[Uproot]].
* '''CompostYieldMultiplier''' = 1.5 with [[compost]], and 1.75 with [[super compost]].
* '''WaterYieldMultiplier''' = 1.15 with [[clean water]] or [[dirty water]].

With maximal buffs, players can expect to receive 9 [[flax]], [[corpse cotton]], [[desert weed]], [[bunny cactus]], [[fibrous pipe cactus]], [[barrel cactus]] or 15 of every other plant per harvest. Subsequent harvests of berry bushes will provide less.

The [[Uproot]] spell (and its upgraded version [[Harvester]]) can be used to harvest crops in a (larger) radius, but it does not work with the [[iron secateurs]], and so may result in a lower yield.

The Harvest XP is modified by the yield as well as other factors, and can be modeled as so:

<code>HarvestXP = ceil((BaseHarvestXP * (1 + Yield * HarvestXpFactor) * GlobalXPModifier) * GlobalReduction)</code>
* '''BaseHarvestXP''' = 8
* '''HarvestXPFactor''' = 1 for tier 1 (Brynmoor), 2 for tier 2 (Ghornfell), and 3 for tier 3 (Fellhollow and Umbral Sands).
* '''GlobalXPModifier''' = 1 for 0% XP Boosts, 1.1 * 1.05 for 15% XP Boosts, 1.1 * 1.05 * 1.15 for 30% XP Boosts, and 1.1 * 1.05 * 1.3 for 45% XP Boosts (Note that these values are multiplicative in formula, but written additively for legibility).
* '''GlobalReduction''' = 1 is the default, 0.05 for subsequent berry-bush harvests.

==Walkthrough==
===Begin your adventure!===
[[File:Wise_Old_Man.png|thumb|150px|Wise Old Man in the Temple]]
Go and speak to the [[Wise Old Man]] in the temple. He will tell you about the dragon and offer to teach you about the basics, which you can either accept or refuse. If you refuse it, you can talk with him again in [[Bramblemead Valley|Bramblemead Village]] to finish the quest. If you accept the tutorial, he will send you to [[Doric]] just outside the temple, starting [[Getting Started]].

=== Before Setting Off... ===
''This step is covered, in more detail, through the following quest articles: [[Getting Started]], [[Ratcatcher]], and [[Rune Mysteries]].''

Doric will teach you how to make processing stations, introduce to you the building system, and then send you off to Vannaka. The slayer master will send you to fight off nearby rats, teach you how to cook your food, and help you know which way the pointy end goes before sending you to Zanik. When you talk to Zanik, she will help you learn the magic system, crafting runes for spells, and even unlock a spell or two. When she has taught you everything, she'll then send you off to the Wise Old Man.

===Finishing up...===
After completing the above section, or if you skipped the tutorial, go to [[Bramblemead Valley|Bramblemead Village]] and find the Wise Old Man on the first floor of a ruined building at the far end of the village. Talk to him to learn about the next step in your adventure.

==Mechanics==
To train this skill, players use a fishing tool with its respective fishing spot. Nets only work on [[net fishing spot]]s and fishing rods only work on [[rod fishing spot]]s.

==== Net Fishing ====
Stand near a net fishing spot with any net equipped. Use the ''Trawl'' action button (default: LMB) to begin to catching fish or junk (like stone or weeds). Each trawl will use 10 stamina.

Unlike rod fishing, trawling only works within the range of a non-depleted fishing spot. Nets can be used in any region, regardless of material, to catch fish.

Attempting to fish in a depleted fishing spot results in a notification that there are no fish here.

==== Rod Fishing ====
Unlike with net fishing, casting requires being at least a certain distance away from the fishing spot. Equip a fishing rod (and optional bait) and use the ''Cast'' action button (default: LMB) to cast towards the fishing spot. This can be held to charge to cast out farther. Should the casting strength be either too weak or strong, it will miss, using no stamina and no bait. Without bait, the chance to catch junk is more likely.

After successfully casting, wait a moment to get a bite from a fish. It will try to swim away and needs to be tired out (with remaining energy shown in the fish bar above the stamina bar). Immediately use the ''Strafe Left/Right'' buttons (default: A/D) to pull the fish in the opposite direction. The fish may change directions; when this happens, the fish bar will turn red and the opposite strafe direction must be used.

Once the fish becomes somewhat tired, the option to reel will appear. To reel in the fish, release the ''Strafe'' button and instead hold same button as the ''Cast'' action. This depletes the fish bar much more quickly. The fish may resume swimming while being reeled in, at which point the ''Cast'' button should be released and ''Strafe'' resumed. Repeat until caught. Pressing the wrong buttons will result in the fish escaping once the player runs out of stamina.

For best fishing effectiveness, it is recommended to equip the region-specific fishing rod and accompanying bait:{{Fact|text=explain why}}

Gathering:
'''Gathering skills''' (or just "gathering") is a category of skills within ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' that allow the players to interact with scenery items to acquire resources or materials.

== Overview ==
While these skills are strictly non-combative in nature, they allow the player to acquire resources that cannot be acquired in massive quantities in a short amount of time or not acquired through monster drops. These skills also have their own special type of tools that enable the player to get experience.

=== Mining ===
Mining is a gathering skill that pertains to mining ore nodes or certain rocks (such as stone boulders and granite deposits) with a pickaxe. At a high enough level, it is possible to acquire gemstones from certain ore nodes while mining.

=== Woodcutting ===
Woodcutting is a gathering skill that pertains to chopping down trees to acquire logs using a logging axe. By creating better logging axes using higher-tiered materials (such as bronze or iron), one can chop down stronger trees and weaker tress faster.

=== Farming ===
Farming is a gathering skill that pertains to growing and harvesting crops. By planting seeds in planters (or tree seeds on the ground), using watering cans, and compost, one can gather specific resources that would otherwise be hard to collect easier. At a high enough level, it is possible to create a higher version of compost and create a tool that creates a small increase to crop yields.

=== Fishing ===
Fishing is a gathering skill that pertains to catching fish in specific fishing spots. By using nets to trawl for fish closer to shore and cast using rods (with bait) to catch fish from far away, one can gather a renewable food source.

* [[Garou druid]]
|qtype = secondary
}}

==Walkthrough==
===Starting off===
Zanik will tell the player they sense the presence of a prophecy in the [[Outlook Ruins]] to the north-east of her, as well as in the [[Adventurer's Guild]] to the south. Both areas are overrun with goblins, so make sure you're properly equipped to take on the challenge with health potions, food, and water.

'''It is recommended that you place a lodestone at Zanik's location, as you'll have to come back to Zanik to complete the quest. This way, you can easily fast travel back to the location.'''

===Bandosian Amulets===
You can choose to either search the nearby ruins first or the Adventurer's Guild first. Both contain a [[reliquary]] containing the Bandosian amulet, but only one can be looted. The amulet in the location you didn't check first ends up stolen by a garou druid.

The ruins' reliquary is tucked away in a corner, whereas the guild reliquary is blocked by thorny vines, requiring 20 [[Woodcutting]] to cut down. The guild is also more dangerous due to the number of goblins inhabiting it, so it's recommended to obtain the amulet from the ruins' reliquary. Both locations have a caged goblin outside. [[Bilegut]] can be found outside the Outlook Ruins, and [[Wormelbow]] can be found outside the Adventurer's Guild. When talking to either of them before obtaining a Bandosian amulet, they'll offer to tell you the exact location of the respective reliquary in exchange for a [[steak]]. This is optional, as the reliquaries can be found without their help.

Next, you'll need to head to whichever location you '''did not''' obtain the Bandosian amulet from. If you obtained the amulet from the ruins, then head to the guild, and if you obtained the amulet from the guild, then head to the ruins. You don't need to defeat all the goblins there—simply locate the caged goblin and eliminate the goblins around it. Once the area is clear, speak with the caged goblin to learn the whereabouts of the second Bandosian amulet. The goblin will reveal that a garou-beastman has taken the second amulet to a cave in the Whispering Swamp.

[[File:Goblin Diplomacy - Lower swamp access point.png|thumb|Location of the bridge to reach the lower area of the swamp]]

Now, you must head to the [[Druid's Cave|cave]] in the swamp where a [[garou druid]] is keeping the second [[Druid's Bandosian Amulet|Bandosian amulet]]. However, the journey is not quite straightforward. '''The cave is located at the very bottom of the swamp''', so be sure you go down into the swamp safely first, and then search for the cave. Otherwise, you will be running above the cave location and won’t be able to find the entrance. Once you've located the cave entrance, enter to find the garou druid. Defeat the garou druid to obtain the second Bandosian amulet. The garou druid is quite strong and can inflict a potent poison. To defeat it more easily, use magic attacks at a distance, and be sure to dodge its poison thorns.

===Returning to Zanik===
After obtaining both Bandosian amulets, return to Zanik. She will thank you for bringing the two amulets, and this will complete the quest. As a reward, Zanik will give you the [[goblin war banner]].

'''Growing Pains''' is a secondary [[Quests|quest]] that is meant to teach the player how to use the [[Farming]] skill.

==Overview==

{{Quest details
|desc = Learn the basics of the Farming skill from the Wise Old Man.

|req = None
|item_req =
* 18 [[ash logs]] to build an [[ash farming plot]], [[wooden spade]], and a [[wooden watering can]]
* 2 [[coarse thread]] to build the Wooden Spade and Wooden Watering Can
* 3 [[wheat seeds]] (acquired during quest)

==Walkthrough==
Make and receive either the [[wooden watering can]] or the [[wooden spade]] in your inventory. This will trigger a quest to start talking to the [[Wise Old Man]] at [[Bramblemead Valley]], where he will give you the basics of the [[Farming]] skill. Ensure that at least one inventory space is available to receive the [[wheat seeds]]. 

===Building a plot===
After talking to the Wise Old Man, create an [[ash farming plot]] and dig the plot whilst wielding the [[wooden spade]]. Dig five times, and you will receive at least three [[weeds]] and 3 Farming experience. It is recommended to store the weeds inside a [[compost bin]] to create compost for future plots. After digging the wheat plot, place the wheat seeds in your inventory (or equip the seeds) and left-click on the plot. You will receive 5 Farming experience for planting the wheat seeds. After spreading the seeds, you will need to water the wheat plot at each stage by equipping a full watering can. You can fill your watering can by pressing the {{Key press|F}} key on a pond of water. Water the wheat plot five times until you see a check mark at the bottom of the watering icon. You will need to wait half an in-game day (12 minutes client-side) for the wheat chute to grow into a wheat stalk. 

Once the wheat chute grows into a wheat stalk, water the plot five times again. At any time during the process, not watering the plant after six in-game hours after the next phase will result in the wheat chute becoming diseased. You will not be able to create [[plant cure]], so you will have to start again. 

After waiting another in-game day, the wheat stalk will turn into harvestable wheat. Harvest the wheat before talking to the Wise Old Man again, and he will reward you with a pack of Farming supplies.

'''Note:''' ''Interacting with the door to the Umbral Sands will play a small introduction cutscene to the region.''

After defeating the Black Knight Titan and talking to Avisk, head back to [[The Bastion]] and interact with the door to the Umbral Sands. ''It is highly recommended that you do this during the night cycle at full rest.'' Once you have interacted with the door, you will arrive at the [[Alcarrid Oasis]] sub-region. Speak to [[Shangruuh - Alcarrid Envoy|Shangruuh]] right as you arrive to start the quest. 

Arriving to the camp, speak to [[Ancamairon - Alcarrid Elder|Ancamairon]], who will next to [[Icthlarin]]. Icthlarin requests one of the [[mirror lens]] they hold in order to use the [[mirrors]] and break the seal that blocks [[Fuzan]]'s [[Fight Cave|tower]]. The garou does not trust an outsider, let alone a demigod, with their sacred item. So you will be asked to gain the trust of the Moon Garou, starting with the Alcarrid camp.

Once you accept the quest, you'll need to speak to certain NPCs to progress.

Speak to any of them to start the tasks needed to convince the elder of the Alcarrid tribe.
