==== The Mirror Crack'd ====
''Item(s) required'': 3 [[adamant bar]]. If mining the materials: a [[mithril pickaxe]] (or better), 9 [[adamantite ore]] and 9 [[coal]].

Speak to [[Valas - The Blacksmith|Valas]], and they will remark about how your task to repair the mirrors smells like folly to them. They commend your spirit, but then tell you how the mirrors are sacred to them because of the [[Elidinis|River Goddess]] placing them there to remind them of who must protect Umbral Sands.

Speak to Valas again when you have the bars. Click on option 1 to hand over the bars, and they will say that they will fix the mirrors for you when you collect all of the lenses. They will inform the elder of your part in getting that job done and give you a nice farewell. They will also give you 200 [[garou chit]] for your troubles.

==== Rag and Bone Garou ====
''Item(s) required'': 3 [[raw farm meat]], 3 [[kalphite shell fragments]], and 3 [[cactus steak]]s

Speak to [[Lagra - The Butcher|Lagra]], who wants you to help them with a task and clarifies that they are a butch (or butcher) and want you to bring them three of the following: [[Raw farm meat]], [[kalphite shell fragments]], and [[cactus steak]]s. You can collect the raw farm meat from nearby vultures, goats, or from your own chests if you have any. The shell fragments can also be found by killing kalphites in the desert or if you have some already. As for cactus steaks, you only need to chop down one or two bunny cactuses with an adamant (or better) logging axe or collect them from your chests.

Speak to Lagra again when you have the items. Choose option 1 to hand over the meats, and they will praise your work by saying that you have an eye for dead tissue and exoskeletons. They will give you their trust and give you 200 garou chit for your troubles.

Once you have completed the three tasks above, return to Ancamairon. He will mention that the Alcarrid clan now trusts you and that the butcher has even made a dish after you. 

'''Reward:''' ''[[Moon Garou pack]] and a new Magic Carpet [[mount]].'' 

After completing the tasks for the Alcarrid clan, you now have to navigate to other areas of the desert to collect their lenses. You can go to either the Manafem clan in the southern area of the desert (within the [[Manafem Plains]]) or the Uzzer clan in the east (within the [[Dunes of Uzzer]]) and speak to their respective elders to discuss building reputation and claiming the lenses.

=== Part II: Manafem Trouble ===
Speak to [[Dúshlánach - Manafem Elder|Dúshlánach]] in the [[Manafem Plains|Manafem]] camp. They will mention that you are a bad omen at a bad time, calling you Unmarked, and reveal they bear the Mark of Fuzan and how that mark is a wound that carves deep. From this Mark, they are slowly losing their will to fight and their sanity, but they do say that their pride is not being lost. They say that while the clan needs help, they are reluctant to accept it. This means that their tasks will be somewhat harder. Just like with the Alcarrid clan, there are three tasks that must be done to acquire their lens.

'''Note:''' ''[[Beartach - The Merchant|Beartach]] will not offer any quests, but completing the reputation quests will increase his reputation by one level.''

==== Song of the Ancients ====
''Item(s) required:'' Good [[weapons]], [[armour]], [[food]] and 5 [[air rune]]<nowiki/>s

Speak to [[Laguna - The Bard|Laguna]], who is sitting next to a net fishing spot. They would like you to venture into [[Dragonkin Vault|the Vault]] located south of the camp and write down the lyrics of the songs as they do not like beetles and heard that beetles reside within the vault.

The vault they spoke of will be circled in green on your map. Be warned that this is a [[kalphite]] nesting area, so you will need to rush to the entrance to avoid being outnumbered by kalphites and [[KotHaar]] that lurk around the area.

Enter the vault door and head towards the next platform. You will need to summon a [[scarab staff]] and take it with you, as this will prevent the scarabs within the dungeon from hurting you. After summoning the staff, the first ancient garou statue will be to the right. Collect this before continuing deeper into the vault. 

You will be in combat sometime, and the staff can be swapped for you to protect yourself, which will allow you to pick the staff back up. In the first room, follow the path that leads to a lever, pull it but to not proceed as east of the lever there is a [[Ancient Garou Statue|ancient garou statue]] for you to transcribe. Follow the path and head into the next room, where the statue will be located on top of a platform, requiring [[Windstep]] to reach. Now that you have acquired all of the lyrics, you ''may'' return to Laguna in the Manafem camp.

'''Note''': ''The next two levers will open the way to one of the [[Kalphite Queen]]<nowiki/>s. If you are prepared, you can enter the encounter to claim extra reward on beating her, such as the [[keris]]' [[vestige]], [[corroded curved blade]].''

Speak to Laguna again and they will be happy that you found them all and wants to weave them into a song. After that, they promise to vouch for you with the Manafem Elder.

==== Scaling Difficulties ====
''Item(s) required'': Good [[weapons]], [[armour]], and [[food]].{{Map|entity=|width=250px|height=250px|center=206772,260417|zoom=3|Scaling Difficulties|float=right}}Speak to [[Hedric - The Hunter|Hedric]], he'll tasks you with looking for his lost scouting party. The scouting party were tracking a creature that had been picking off his people one by one and asks you to look for them towards the east and kill the beast.

After talking with [[Hedric - The Hunter|Hedric]], head towards the green area on your map east from the Manafem camp. Within that area, there will be three clues in the area, two dead garou scouts and a scorched mark. You'll learn that the scouting party is dead, and Neither the [[Scorch]], the sandstorms or Fuzan could have made them, but something else. Head further east to where the green circle is on your map and you will find a [[red dragon]]. Kill it and gain [[the radiant heart]]. 

Head back to [[Hedric - The Hunter|Hedric]] and speak with him and you will recount how you found their bodies and slain the red dragon nearby. He will thank you for finding their bodies and, that now you made it safe, will send someone to go collect their bodies. He will remark that the dragon you slain is small-fry compared to Fuzan, hopes you know what your doing, and recommended you to their Elder. He will give you 200 garou chit for your troubles. 

==== Beast in the Sand ====
Item(s) required: 1 [[clean water]].

Speak to [[Manathep - The Bereaved|Manathep]] and she will tell you about how the [[Dearg Due]] killed her poor [[Efina - The Lost|Efina]]. She mentions that Efina was taken three days ago and every night, the Dearg Due watches her from the south of their camp with a glint in her eye and blood on her lips. She asks you to kill the Dearg Due south of the camp and bring back Efina's body.

Head west of the pyramid vault and track down the Dearg Due in the sandstorm. Follow it until you meet Efina. Speak to her and she will ask for clean water. Give her some clean water and she will say that her strength is coming back to her while thanking you. she then reveals that she ran away from the Manafem camp due to the Mark of Fuzan draining everyone. She then asks you to tell her mum that she is safe and on her way back. The Dearg Due howls back, but you get the sense that a curse has been lifted and the Dearg Due is free to move on from this world.

Return to speak to Manathep. She will praise the River Goddess in joy that her daughter is safe and thinks that the Dearg Due lured her out of the camp as a trick and says the Efina wouldn't go out there alone. She will then give you 200 garou chit for your troubles.

Once you have completed these tasks, speak again to Dúshlánach.

'''Reward:''' ''Level 4 reputation with [[Beartach - The Merchant]]'s shop, 1 [[mirror lens]], and a [[Moon Garou pack]].''

=== Part III: Heart of Uzzer ===
Speak to [[Gaimbín - Uzzer Elder|Gaimbín]] within the [[Dunes of Uzzer]], who will doubt your skills and warns you to leave as they needed to prepare for the event of Fuzan's Marking. Of course you'll be once again tasked to gain the clan's trust in order for the elder to reward you with the mirror lens.

==== The Dig Site ====
{{Map|The Dig Site|height=250px|width=250px|zoom=3|center=178805.900521,370596.933689|float=right}}
''Item(s) required'': 1 [[spade]] of any kind, good [[weapons]], [[armour]] and [[food]] to defend yourself from the [[KotHaar]].

Speak to [[Lehran - The Archaeologist|Lehran]] who asks that you help him learn the truth of his ancestors and he will vouch for you with the elder. He tells you that there are some ruins to the far south, long lost to the sands, and that the KotHaar have prevented him from travelling there himself. He reveals that the Forbidden Scrolls are meant to tell the truth about what happened to the Moon Garou centuries ago and not the stuff fed to them by their Elders. He asks for you to go dig them up and bring back the scrolls to him, offering to also share the revelations with you if there are any.

Head to the area marked on your map, with your spade in your inventory/hotbar. In order to find the scrolls, you will need to locate areas that are similar to buried chests. Each Forbidden Scroll will be in one specific ruin with two of them hidden behind locked gates. As there will be KotHaar and goats in the area, you will have to fight them in order to dig peacefully. There are four scrolls you will need to find and they are the following:

* 'The Schism'
* 'Sun Demon'
* Old Kingdom'
* 'Moon Goddess'

Once you have all four scrolls, return to Lehran. Give him the scrolls and he will then give you 200 garou chit for your troubles.

==== Saga of the Adventurer ====
{{Map|Saga of the Adventurer|height=250px|width=250px|zoom=1|center=59009.2,351799.1|float=right}}
''Item(s) requires'': 1 [[torch]], good [[weapons]], [[armour]] and [[food]] to better defend yourself against wandering enemies.

Speak to [[Laguna - The Bard|Laguna]] and they will tell you that they are on the market for a business partner and one with survival skills. They will tell you that there are four rocky spires around the pyramid close to this camp and that each spire holds a statue. They will ask you to go find each statue and note down the inscribed passages. Each passage, woven together, will form a saga. They will give you a book and reminds you to note down the passages at the rocky spires.

Head towards the area marked on your map. You will find that there are towering rocky spires around the area of the Pyramid and you must interact with them. Some of these statues will be hidden in caves blocked by sandstone nodes and others will be protected by either KotHaar or kalphites. Inspect each statue to gain a piece of the saga. Once you have collected enough pieces of the saga, you will then need to follow a direction pointing towards a specific direction. Head towards the spire with the [[Nightmare Crucible|Nightmare Crucible of Humilitation]] entrance and there will be the last ancient garou statue containing the full saga.

Once you have the complete saga, return to Laguna. They will congratulate you on finishing the saga and would enjoy performing at Fuzan's Mark Day, but for now, they will sing praises of your deeds to the elder. They also remark that you are free to unlock and explore the gateways as you see fit.

'''Note:''' ''You will gain a Crucible Engram of Humiliation for completing this segment.''

=== Part IV: Fuzan Trials ===
''Item(s) required'': Good [[weapons]], [[armour]], and [[food]].

''Visit [[Fuzan/Strategies]] for a guide to fighting Fuzan.''

Speak to Icthlarin and he will say that there is little time to waste and that we must repair the mirrors. He informs you that he has positioned them carefully and believes they are directed at Fuzan's Lens, which is a dragonkin relic that protects both his volcano and powers his Mark. That belief, he says, will be tested now and prays to Elidnis for help if he's wrong. '''Imaru the Soul-Eater''' is an [[undead]] blue [[Dragon (race)|dragon]] infused with the [[wild anima]] of [[Ashenfall]] and the energy of the {{RSL|Underworld}} by drinking from the {{RSL|River Noumenon}}{{CiteVideo|author=IGN|title=RuneScape: Dragonwilds - Fellhollow Expansion Official Cinematic Narrative Trailer|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oWA7tSeCf0M|timestamp=|date=14 December 2025|site=YouTube|name=imaru}}. She was one of [[Kuldra]]'s generals, who rules over [[Fellhollow]], a boss monster who was introduced with the 0.10 update.

[[Imaru's Tower]] is located within [[Hope's Fall]], a region of [[Fellhollow]]. The entrance to the tower is sealed with magic. For the player to enter her lair, they have to find three curse fragments and use them to dispel the barrier that prevents entry. If you have faced Imaru (and defeated her), you will need to re-collect all of the curse fragments to unlock the magical seal. Unlike [[Velgar]]'s world events, Imaru only attacks the player out in the world if they are soul-rifting for too long.

==History==
===Early life===
Like all other dragons in Ashenfall, Imaru was created by the [[Dragonkin (race)|dragonkin]]. Imaru was a water dragon, infused with water magic by the dragonkin who created her. Though the rage characteristic of her kind burned within her, her elemental nature tempered it, granting her the reason and clarity that would define her disposition.{{CiteJournal|journal=Imaru|quote=Although the dragon's rage still burned inside her, the cooling power of the water she was infused with, calmed her and brought the reason and clarity that she enjoyed.}} The dragonkin's experiments had denied her the ability to bear offspring, the one thing she desired above all else.{{CiteJournal|journal=Imaru's Head|quote=Cruel dragonkin experiments had robbed her of the only thing she had ever wanted, to be a mother.}}

She and her mate, [[Xikotal]], settled within the region of Fellhollow. When human settlers found their way to the region, it was Imaru who persuaded Xikotal that they should take the settlers under their protection, seeing in the fragile humans the children she could never have.{{CiteJournal|journal=Imaru|quote=she convinced Xikotal that they should take them under their wing, becoming protectors and, perhaps, even parents to the fragile things.}} The two dragons at first kept their distance from the settlers,{{CiteJournal|journal=Lazilly-Penned Diary|quote=You'd think they'd be cruel landlords, given that they're dragons and all. After them beast people turned on our Southern neighbours and wiped them all out, you'd expect these dragons to do the same. They was working together after all.

But, no, that's not how it goes. Or at least not how it's going. The two of them kept their distance at first, pretending we weren't here. We watched as the flight of dragons swept over us and ignored us altogether, fearing the side eyes from our two new friends.}} but later befriended them.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lazilly-Penned Diary|quote=Then, when it were all over and done with, here they were. Talking to us, as though we were neighbours. Speaking to us as though we were friends.}} Imaru and Xikotal helped their new friends build cities, farmland, and control the weather.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lazilly-Penned Diary|quote=Her magic brought rain and his calmed the winds, so that our harvests were plentiful, and our population bloomed. All it costs is a few sheep or cows every once in a while, a pretty good deal if you ask me}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Second Journal|quote=these dragons watch over the villagers, help them with construction, farming, all sorts of stuff.}} Those whom she and Xikotal protected were given a blessing, an enchantment woven over each of the settlers.{{CiteJournal|journal=Dragon-Embossed Journal|quote=Gran says that's what the Blessing is, that little dragon magic in our bones. An enchantment woven over each of us, as part of the dance. It makes us healthier, makes us heartier, makes us better than before.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Captain Rainer's Journal|quote=Since most of us had not undergone this so-called "Blessing",}} She also appointed guards to protect her and Xikotal when they went into long torpors.{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Sword|quote=She was chosen by Imaru as one of her guards, not that a dragon needed such a thing, and she was responsible for the defense of the dragons when they fell into the weeks-long torpors they were known to suffer.}}

After the [[Dragon Rebellion]], Kuldra had issued an extermination order against the human settlements in Ashenfall, minus a few. She took notice of Imaru's and Xikotal's mercy. Finding this a betrayal, she descended onto the region to handle it herself.{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Sword|quote=When Kuldra descended on the region, demanding humanity's destruction,}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Platelegs|quote=When Kuldra arrived it was as if the air had grown heavy, pressing down on everyone. A whole village fell silent as the Godeater turned her gaze upon them.}} Imaru and Xikotal denied Kuldra, rejecting her demands and rising against her, and the humans rose with them.{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Platelegs|quote=As Imaru and Xikotal rose to face her, villagers instinctively ran to don their heirloom steel armour, hoping that they wouldn't have to use it, but knowing in their hearts that they would.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Sword|quote=She was chosen by Imaru as one of her guards, not that a dragon needed such a thing, and she was responsible for the defense of the dragons when they fell into the weeks-long torpors they were known to suffer.}} But even with numbers on their side, Kuldra proved too powerful. Imaru witnessed her mate's heart ripped from his chest and devoured by Kuldra.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=I have a new customer, and she won't fit through the door.
Odd to empathise with a dragon, but I do. We all saw what happened. I watched as the great multi-headed dragon queen pulled Xikotal's heart from his chest and ate it in front of his mate.}} Instead of killing Imaru, Kuldra left her to her grief, considering this punishment enough for disobeying her.

Imaru sought out [[Ravanna]], a sorcerer who had practised in the magical arts, including necromancy.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Second Journal|quote=I set up a little shop. Can you imagine? Me, with a shop! Just selling little potions and salves, and services for those that need to speak with the dead.}} She begged for her beloved back, but Ravanna declined, as she was not powerful enough to reanimate things to that degree.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=After the death of her mate she came to me seeking a way to bring him back. Necromancy doesn't work like that, at least not yet and certainly not within my skill set.}} Instead, she offered a different solution: a curse to allow Imaru to take vengeance on Kuldra.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=Curses, though, that I'm good with those.

Imaru's rage makes her the perfect focus. The beating heart around the darkest magics. She can be a weapon against the Godeater,}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=thought I could offer her something almost as good. I offered her revenge. I created a curse within her, using her grief and rage as a focus, so that it might strengthen her against Kuldra.}} Ravanna bestowed a curse that would turn Imaru's grief into power, a blade intended for the Godeater.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=he rage of a dragon, combined with the power of a grief-curse, such a thing could be the blade needed to slit Kuldra's throat.}}

Armed with the curse, Imaru attacked Kuldra a second time. Witnesses described a battle of catastrophic force, the land itself weaponised as the two dragons tore at one another.{{CiteJournal|journal=Weathered Journal|quote=Imaru and Kuldra, raging against one another using Ashenfall as a weapon. The wind became knives, the rocks hurled as cannon-fire, and the rain turned to hail, falling like great-hammers on everyone caught in their path.}} The curse had changed her; her grief and rage had been forged into something that shook even Kuldra's armour.{{CiteJournal|journal=Weathered Journal|quote=She feels different this time, Imaru. Changed. Like her grief and her rage have been forged into weapons and she slams them against the Godeater with unbridled hate. In response, Kuldra laughs, even though her armour shudders against the force of it, scales falling to the earth like the beginning flakes of winter snow.}} As Imaru pressed the attack, the Blessing began drawing strength from the villagers themselves, leaving those who bore it weakened.{{CiteJournal|journal=Weathered Journal|quote=There is a sensation in my chest -- strength being leeched from within me as Imaru presses the attack. I see old Mrs. Mossfoot stumble, hand across her chest, as each of the other villagers feel it too. The Blessing, a source of strength, now feels like a hole in each of us, draining us dry.}} Despite everything, Kuldra proved too powerful and killed her.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=So Imaru died. Fell to the ground in a crumbled heap}} However, due to the very curse put on her, Imaru did not give up. She instead wedged herself, preventing herself from moving on drinking from the '''River Noumenon''' and clawed her way out of the underworld, resurrecting herself to continue her vengeance, though that came with a cost: corruption.<ref name="imaru" /> Imaru caused the river to become blocked,{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fifth Journal|quote=Things are so much worse than I thought. The River Noumenon, the way to the Afterlife, is blocked}} with its waters beginning to leak into the surface of Fellhollow.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fifth Journal|quote=She claws at the edge of the Underworld, creating rifts that bleed the Noumenon's waters into our world like some deadly poison that rips out the soul.}} This gave her a hunger for souls. She gave into it, feasting on those she had sworn to protect and turning them into undead.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fifth Journal|quote=She uses her "Blessing" as an anchor to her people, dragging their souls to her so that she might feast and grow stronger.

So focused on strength and power, on beating Kuldra, that she doesn't think about what happens to everyone else. My soul is protected, warded by the curse that rages inside me, but the other villagers aren't so lucky.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Sixth Journal|quote=The necromantic energies of the Underworld then wash back through the Blessing and into her subjects, animating their bodies and filling them with an unquenchable thirst for more souls. They're nothing but withered husks of themselves, all humanity drained away and all that's left is a terrible, clawing, need.}} Soon this rot began spreading further, and even those who had not been blessed began becoming undead,{{CiteJournal|journal=Captain Rainer's Journal|quote=Since most of us had not undergone this so-called "Blessing", we thought we were safe from this terrifying transformation}} as the necrotic magic infected those bitten.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ulgo's Diary|quote=Fun game. '''Queen Kuldra''', also known as the '''Dragon Queen''' and the '''God Eater''', is an ancient black [[Dragon (race)|dragon]] with five heads. She is the leader of the dragons ruling over the continent of [[Ashenfall]], and the current '''High Queen''' for some of the [[Garou (race)|garou]].{{CiteJournal|journal=Garou Highborn's Cloak|quote=Even after turning from the moon-goddess Lougrim, becoming servants of the High Queen Kuldra, the garou continue their ancient rituals.}} She is the boss of the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid, and the final boss for Kuldra's Saga.

==History==
===Creation===
Kuldra was amongst the first dragons created by the [[Dragonkin (race)|dragonkin]] [[Lacrussa]] and [[Avisk]]. When Lacrussa was working on making a better race of dragons, Avisk would force himself into her experiments and suggesting to fuse certain dragons for a better results.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=Avisk is like the scales behind my wings, irritating and in desperate needs of a good scratch. He keeps coming to me and trying to explain to me how I need to do X with the dragons, or Y with their eggs, as if he, an Aughra, has the slightest understanding of real science. Imbecile.}} He would mess with some of the brood, adding [[rune essence]] into the them.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=He's already messed with some of the brood, tried to use that strange rune essence in ways that would cause energy to flow in certain ways. I can see the concept he's going for, but his clumsy nonsense just leads it to ruin.}} Despite Lacrussa's warning in trying to maintain a single headed dragons, Avisk ignored her, which led to several of these brood to die, all but one.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=Trying to create some sort of enhanced mind for the dragons, as if they could exist like a swarm. All of them, of course, died. All but one, and she's turned out strangely}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=I encourage the growth of a single head for the dragons, keeps them sane and stable. There's no good that can come from multiple brains in charge of one body, yet she proves me wrong.}} Kuldra was born showing no signs of madness for having multiple minds. Instead she found that it would work as one, unified in a way.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=All the minds work as if connected, as if part of the same whole. A single consciousness spread across all of them. A single personality.}} Lacrussa learns that the dragon was able to spread the rage across herself, weakening the effect, causing her to express other emotion and behaviours, such as curiosity, reason and even wit.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=Because that’s what it is, a personality. A will. A mind of her own. She is enraged, yes, like all dragons are, but she spreads it across herself, weakening the effect. I have encountered curiosity, reason, even wit.}} This would make Lacrussa want to study her further, keeping her chained. During the study, they would get her off springs and conduct several experiments on them, exterminating the failures.{{CiteVideo|author=RuneScape: Dragonwilds|title=Scorned Wilderness - Narrative Trailer {{!}} RuneScape: Dragonwilds|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cA6J1J5s9X0|timestamp=0:37|site=YouTube|date=10 September 2026}} Kuldra would witness this, and slowly plot her vengeance.

===Dragon Rebellion===
After the [[Human-Garou War]], the [[Gods|goddess]] [[Lougrim]] donated her blood to the dragonkin for their assistance against the human and [[Bandos|bandosians]]{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Notes|quote=One of them bleeds. Perhaps all of them, but this one for certain. She calls herself a goddess of the moon and the primordial hunt. Nonsense, of course, moons are rocks floating in the emptiness and there's nothing spiritual or metaphysical about a predator seeking lunch. Still, if I can refine this power? If I can merge it with a dragon, perhaps… just perhaps… I can turn these worthless dragons into something we can use.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Sanguine Urn|quote=The dragonkin discovered a unique and powerful resources in their time on Ashenfall, the blood of a goddess - Lougrim. She was a moon deity, in-tune with the natural world, the forest and a source of great vitality. Her blood carries some of those properties.}}. Lacrussa would use this on Kuldra. After gaining Lougrim's blood, she would plot a [[Dragon Rebellion|rebellion]] against the dragonkin after seeing the continued abuse, despite their assistance in the war. At first, she was hesitant, but it was [[Velgar]] who convinced her and was the first to join her cause. When the rebellion started, Lacrussa was slain, along with [[Brakka]], from whom Kuldra stole powers for herself and shared them with Velgar, her most trusted ally,{{CiteJournal|journal=Velgar|quote=General Velgar was one of Kuldra's most trusted allies in the dragon rebellion. In the years that led to the betrayal of their Dragonkin masters, she would seek Velgar's advice on how to best handle the situation. His answer was always clear, brutality was the only language that their masters would understand.}} granting him his elemental mastery of earth.{{CiteJournal|journal=Fractured Cape|quote=Kuldra, the godeater, crushed him beneath her great claw and feasted on his anima-rich soul. Stealing Brakka’s power for herself. She gifted Velgar, her most trusted general, with the elemental mastery of the fallen Nodon architect.}} Before she could kill [[Rasthin]], the dragonkin, activated the [[Harmonic Resonator]] in hope to destroy Kuldra, only for the Dragon Queen to survive. In a battle that fractured the continent itself,{{CiteText|text=Leathery Parchment|quote=The battle was swift and bloody; their clashing energies created cracks in the very earth. The entire continent buckled beneath their fury, but only one of them could prevail.}} Kuldra then attacked Lougrim, who was protecting the garou village. Weak and wounded, Kuldra descended on her without mercy and devouring her body and taking her title of High Queen of the Garou. Some accepted out of fear, but others rejected her rule and left to another region. Having freed her fellow dragons, she sent them out across the continent to wipe out other settlements, other than the garou and [[Goblin (race)|goblins]].

Sometime during these events, Kuldra caught wind of [[Imaru]]'s and [[Xikotal]]'s mercy towards the human settlements in [[Fellhollow]], and as a result, she decided to confront the duo herself. As Kuldra descended on the region, nobles within the region would arm themselves in [[steel equipment]]{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Platelegs|quote=When Kuldra arrived it was as if the air had grown heavy, pressing down on everyone. A whole village fell silent as the Godeater turned her gaze upon them. As Imaru and Xikotal rose to face her, villagers instinctively ran to don their heirloom steel armour, hoping that they wouldn‘t have to use it, but knowing in their hearts that they would.}} to assist Xikotal and Imaru, in the hope of defending their new home and bring an end to the Dragon Queen. Despite the help and numbers, they failed to bring Kuldra down. With Kuldra's strength and power seemingly unmatched, she would pull Xikotal's heart from his chest and devour it.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=I have a new customer, and she won’t fit through the door.
Odd to empathise with a dragon, but I do. We all saw what happened. I watched as the great multi-headed dragon queen pulled Xikotal’s heart from his chest and ate it in front of his mate.}} She would then leave Imaru to grieve, as punishment for disobeying her.{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Platelegs|quote=After Xikotal’s death, Kuldra left the region, leaving Imaru to her grief.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Battered Diary|quote=She does not end Imaru's pain, not yet. She leaves her with the agony of loss and the dissolution of her dreams for the future. A cruel punishment, for the simple crime of peace. She dared to shelter the lost and wandering humans, rather than to put us to the flames.}} However, Imaru would challenge Kuldra a second time, after being infused by a curse{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=the rage of a dragon, combined with the power of a grief-curse, such a thing could be the blade needed to slit Kuldra’s throat.}} placed by [[Ravanna]].{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=Curses, though, that I’m good with those.

Imaru’s rage makes her the perfect focus. The beating heart around the darkest magics. She can be a weapon against the Godeater,}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=thought I could offer her something almost as good. I offered her revenge. I created a curse within her, using her grief and rage as a focus, so that it might strengthen her against Kuldra.}} However, this was not enough to even stand a chance against Kuldra, who killed her quite easily.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=So Imaru died. Fell to the ground in a crumbled heap}} Despite Imaru's action, Kuldra had left the humans of Fellhollow alone, their fate met by the resurrected corpse of Imaru some time later.

With Ashenfall settlement destroyed, minus some of the garou and [[goblins]], Kuldra now rules the continent with her dragons.

===Sixth Age===
During the 14th Year of the [[Sixth Age]], while ruling unchallenged, an expedition had made its way to Ashenfall; her generals had attacked the expedition in her name. After the arrival of a group of [[Player Character|adventurers]], Kuldra would start gathering pieces of the Harmonic Resonator to cause another explosion that would devour the world. Before she could put her plan into motion and put an end to the world, the adventurer(s) made their way into her sanctum and, through a grueling barrage of her hatchlings trying to protect her from the intruders, was unable to survive after they destroyed her heart.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|Kuldra's tale is tragic really. An innocent child, raised by monsters: tormented, tortured, and forced to create legions of children who were all taken from her and then either weaponised or dissected for future study.

She found comfort in the gentle warmth of a lover's embrace, only to see him taken from her by those same cruel parents.

Only one dragonkin ever showed her warmth, but their mind was distracted by thousand different timestreams and they could never give Kuldra the love that she deserved. A lack of love is like a poison: it seeps into one's soul and infects it with malice. You find yourself unable to believe that love could be real, and from it all the other positive emotions, such as charity, kindness, or hope.

Kuldra wasn't born a monster, but she chose to become one and she was determined to be the worst monster she could be.

For centuries she has gorged herself on the anima of Ashenfall, building her own power so that she might turn the region's wellspring into a weapon that would decimate the rest of the world. Why? Because the rest of the world is happy, and she needs to see that stopped. Now, she is dead - although her legacy will scar the world for generations to come. Hate breeds only hate, and Kuldra has had plenty of children.}}

==Trivia==
* Her appearance from the concept art, banner image and the animated trailers shows some resemblance to {{wp|Tiamat (Dungeons & Dragons)|Tiamat}}, the goddess of greed and queen of evil dragons.
** Just like Tiamat, Kuldra is the Dragon Queen, has 5 heads of different types of dragons, has divinity in her and is worshipped.
** Her appearance in the Fellhollow cutscene intro showed her only having two legs. In ''{{RSL|RuneScape}} (RS3)'', {{RSL|Gorvek}} is another dragon known to also have only two legs.
*** However, her more recent appearance in the Umbral Sands cutscene shows she has all four legs.
* Within the lore of ''RuneScape,'' another dragon is known to exists with the title of Queen; the {{RSL|Queen Black Dragon}}, being the first dragon ever created, and is the ancestor to all dragons.
** Like the Queen Black Dragon, Kuldra is consider the first "perfect" creation, also had children, who were experimented on or enslaved by the dragonkin.
* Kuldra is amongst the few known dragons with multiple heads in the ''RuneScape'' franchise, with the others being the {{RSL|King Black Dragon}} and {{RSL|Verak Lith}}.
** There previously was another {{RSL|Dragon (Learning the Ropes)|three-headed dragon}} in ''RuneScape'', but it was removed along with the tutorial it appeared in.
** {{RSL|Royal dragon|Royal dragons}} are three headed dragons from the {{RSL|Player-owned farm}}, which are a shiny breed of dragons.
* Just like the King Black Dragon and Verak Lith, Kuldra's central head is that of a black dragon.
* She is the only monster in the game with over 10,000 health points.
** This is due to how many times players have to use the anima cannons which each deal 9,999 damage per shot.

==Walkthrough==
===Lending a hand...===
Speak to Postie Pete and select '''option 2''' to talk about this quest. He will ask you (while making a bone pun) if you can help him with something. Accepting his question, Postie Pete will mention how, by RPDT standards, he made a big mistake by misplacing some posts. He will tell you that, as he looked in his bag, someone came by and nabbed three letters. This mysterious thief then fled into Fellhollow. He then tells you that, after taking a quick look, he noticed someone shifty near the little house just outside the entrance to Fellhollow. He will then ask you to take a look for him.

===The Missing Postage===
{{Needed|recommended=Lodestone access to Fellhollow; Food, drink, and gear}}

Walk slightly north-east of the entrance to Fellhollow (where you find Ravanna's third journal) and you will find a suspicious skeleton sitting down in a chair. Talk to it and you will find that they are animate in a similar manner to Postie Pete. They mention being bone idle for the moment and hating puns, but asks you what you want. You have the following options:

Click on '''option 3''', the skeleton will reveal that they haven't gotten any letters. This little ''accidental'' reveal will give you more dialogue options.

From this point, the skeleton will continue to gaslight you. They will say that you had already mentioned it before (No, you didn't) and, thus, open up new dialogue options. Choose '''option 1''' in this new dialogue and the gaslighting continues. By choosing '''option 1''' one more time, the skeleton will concede the gaslighting fight and give you one of the letters. Take this letter to a nearby red deposit box northwest of [[Vannaka|Vannaka's]] camp in [[Bleakfields Valley]] and deliver it.

Upon delivering it, a dialogue box will open up to inform you that when you posted the letter, you found a strange leaf that appears to partially fade into the spirit realm. It will then hint to you going into a spectral door.

'''Note:''' ''This will make the Suspicious Skeleton turn into uninteractable scenery once you acquire the letter from them. The relevant postage deposit box will vanish upon closing out of the dialogue box.''

=== The Spectral Postage ===
Head directly east of [[Cathan|Cathan's]] location (at the [[standing stones]]) to a glowing wall torch with a letter mail satchel dangling down. Interact with it to acquire one of the missing letters. This letter will want you to deliver it to the standing stones in Bleakfields Valley. Immediately head towards Cathan's location and, before going up to see him, the red mail deposit box will be on the left side of the trail. Deliver the postage and a dialogue option will appear. It will tell you that you discovered a small patch of ghostly looking fluff and it looks like unspun wool. This will prompt you to look for the former owner.

=== The Wooly Letter ===
Find a ghostly sheep named "Shaun" to retrieve a ghostly letter. He will be almost directly west of where the last postage deposit box was. Upon receiving the letter, you must take the letter to Imaru's Tower. ''As there are plenty of Rotsworn undead here, you will need to be careful.''

Upon arriving at Imaru's Tower, another red postage deposit box will be in front of her tower off to the right. When you deliver the letter you obtained from Shaun, you will then need to return to Postie Pete. When you choose the option to continue the quest, Pete will thank you to delivering the letters and introduce you to the numbskull who caused the problem in the first place. It turns out that said numbskull was, in fact, Postie Pete's sibling and junior RPDT employee [[Parcel Pete]]. While Parcel Pete wanted to help out, it bungled everything up. Postie Pete will inform you that, due to Parcel Pete's "help", he put him on report and filing his PIP. He will then give you a decorative item that, in the future, will enable you to render further aid to him delivering letters.




'''Congratulations! Quest Complete!'''

'''Magic''' is one of the [[skills]] in ''Runescape: Dragonwilds'' and was released in [[Update:Update 1 - 0.8.0|Update 0.8]].  Magic is one of the three combat styles players can use.  [[Combat]] spells can be cast to efficiently fight monsters from a distance, whereas utility spells have numerous uses.

In addition, players can gain experience from [[Tome of magic|Magic Skill Tomes]] and special reward tomes like the [[Tome of the Dragon Slayer]].

==Equipment==
===Weapons===
[[Magic weapon]]s currently consist of staffs and more recently wands, of which there are several varieties.  Staffs provide a passive rune damage multiplier to provide additional damage.  Staffs are a two-handed weapon; thus, players '''cannot''' equip [[shields]] while wielding staffs. Wands however, can be used in tandem with a shield.

===Armour===
Players can earn set bonuses when wearing armour of the same combat type (i.e., melee, ranged, magic) and can mix and match within that type. For example, a player wearing a [[ranger hat]] (ranged), [[dragonkin mage robes]] (magic), and [[necromancer's robe bottom]] (magic) will get the second tier of magic set bonuses and the first tier of ranged set bonuses. The magic armour set bonuses are:

* 1/3 -50% stamina regen delay
* 2/3 +17.5% magic attack speed
* 3/3 +15% magic crit chance

===Runes===
[[Runes]] are used when casting spells.  Currently, only [[air rune]]s, water runes and [[fire rune]]s can be used for combat magic.  Players can select which [[elemental rune]] they want to autocast by going to the second tab of the inventory and right-clicking on the desired rune.

[[Magical Focus]] is a craftable item unlocked at level 39 '''Magic''' where players can imbue their equipped [[Weapons#Battlestaves|staff]] with a 15% damage multiplier for 10 minutes.

==Utility spells==
{{Main|Spells}}
[[File:Interface - Spells Menu.png|thumb|right|The Spell Book menu.]]
Players unlock utility spells by levelling various [[skills]], including but not limited to Magic. Some utility spells can assist with combat, while other spells are strictly used for skilling or gathering materials more quickly.

===Spellbook (menu)===
[[File:Interface - Quick Spells.png|thumb|200x200px|A Spellbook wheel.]]
Players can access the Spell Book menu by pressing the {{Key press|P}}-button (default).

The left half of the menu shows a list of available/unavailable utility spells. Unavailable spells are greyed out, meaning the player has not met the skill requirement to unlock the spell. Players can hover over the icon for a description of each spell.

The right half of the menu shows the spellbook players can customise with up to 12 utility spells they have unlocked. Players can drag-and-drop or point-and-click the desired utility spells to the spellbook. Players can also cycle between four different spellbooks for added customisation.

===Spellbook (wheel)===
Players can access their customised spellbooks by pressing the {{Key press|Q}}-button (default), which will open the wheel whilst still seeing the player's surroundings. Players can cycle between their four spellbook loadouts and point-and-click the desired utility spell, which will automatically exit the interface.

==Boosts==
Players can consume [[potions]], eat [[food]], or equip [[trinkets]] to increase Magic experience received or damage dealt.

Unlike most other [[skills]] however, there are no '''Magic''' experience potions.

* [[Lesser Magic Potion]] - Increases the chance of landing critical hits with magic by 25% for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Sweet veg ball]] - Grants a 10% XP boost for 5 minutes (300 seconds)
* [[Wild pie]] - Grants a 10% XP boost for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Inspiring amulet of Magic]] - Provides a 5% XP boost to Magic while worn
* [[Glazed pumpkin sandwich]] - provides 10% XP boost for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Amulet of Magic]] - Increases magic damage by 12.5% while worn
* [[Unholy Symbol|Unholy symbol]] - Increases all damage by 15% while lowering maximum HP by 15 points.
* [[Amulet of glory]] - Increases critical damage to all combat style

Mirror, Mirror:
'''Mirror, Mirror''' is a secondary quest in Fellhollow where you must talk to the [[mirror]] to start the quest.

==Overview==
{{Quest details
|desc = Help free a mysterious figure from their mirror prison.
|item_req =
* 1 [[silver bar]]
* 1 [[fine thread]]
* 1 [[sacred oil]]
* 6 [[soul fragment]]
* [[Dragon blood]]
|qtype = secondary
|req = 
* Partial completion of [[Withering Heights]] for access to Fellhollow.
|start = Speak to the [[mirror]] west of the [[Emberwood]] Village
|enemies =
* Multiple [[undead]]
* Either [[green dragon]]s or [[dragon wolf]]
* Multiple Garou
* Multiple Goblins
|rec=
* Good [[armour]] and [[weapons]]
}}

==Walkthrough==
{{Map|Mirror Mirror}}

===A Mysterious Mirror...===
To begin this quest, speak to the [[mirror]] west of the Emberwood Village past the green dragon. You will hear crying audio when you first approach them.

They will be surprised to see a real living person in Fellhollow since their imprisonment decades ago and recount how a terrible necromancer sealed them within the mirror. While this necromancer first taunted them with the ritual needed to release them, they claim it is simple to do and shouldn't take long. They will ask you to collect the required items for them to start the ritual.

For the ritual, they need some [[dragon blood]], a copy of their spellbook found within Emberwood Village, and some spectral silver thread.

'''Note:''' You can kill the nearby green dragon or some dragon wolves for the dragon blood.

===Part I: Reagent Collection===
For the copy of their spellbook, go into Emberwood Village (you will need to either have gotten past this point in the Withering Heights quest or reactivated the statues on a new world) and find the destroyed windmill. Inside, you will find a bedraggled spellbook. Pick this up as you will need it.

For the spectral silver thread, you will need to go find [[Edna|Edna's]] skeleton within [[Dragon's Run]]. To find that, look for a crumbling stone house near a willow grove and a rundown gateway. Her skeleton will be sitting back to a corner on the right side. Interact with the skeleton and the spirit of [[Edna]] will inform you that, to make the spectral silver thread, you will need to bring them the following items:

* 1 [[silver bar]]
* 1 fine thread
* 1 [[sacred oil]]
* 6 [[soul fragment]]s

Once you have all these items, bring them back to [[Edna]]. Once you hand over the ingredients, the skeleton will perform a series of gestures which will be too quick for you to follow with your eyes. After a moment, the skeleton will hand you the spectral silver thread and return to rest. Once that is done, head back to the mirror.

===Part II: The Candles===
Speak to the figure in the mirror once again, and they will be happy that you collected all of the reagents. While they will take them off your hands, they mention that you can press them up to the glass, and they will get them. Hand over the reagents, and they will remark about how, while they prepare the ritual on their side, they will need you to tether them back to your reality by rekindling their memories. The reason why is that, due to their age, they have too many memories and need to put some of them safely away. They left a few of their memories as memorial candles within each region they have visited and, for each candle lit, a memory will return to help anchor them into reality. The figure will give you a small piece of their soul to help ignite these memorial candles and, once each candle is lit, they will be to return.

This is where you will need to visit each region of Ashenfall to light the candles. On your map, the candle areas will be highlighted blue. Here is the list of each candle location within the regions:

* '''Fellhollow:''' Right next to the mirror.
* '''Ghornfell:'''
** '''Fractured Plains:''' Next to a small lake south-south-east of Velgar's Rise. The lake will contain floating rune essence.
** '''Stormtouched Highlands:''' A bit north-east of the garou castle at the edge of a cliff. It will be along the edge of the territory.
** '''Bloodblight Swamp:''' West of the garou encampment leading towards the bloodwood tree.
* '''Brynmoor:'''
** '''Whispering Swamp:''' Next to a giant swamp tree on the third most western island from the vault.
** '''Bramblemead Valley:''' South of the [[Crasorak Kara]] vault, atop the cliff and behind the rocks.

With the final memory candle lit, head back to the mirror.

===Part III: A Week-long Ride===
Speak to the figure in the mirror, and it will inform you that it will get started on the ritual, but their freedom will take roughly a week or so. While you could wait to see what happens, they inform you that you don't need to stick around that long. You have done everything needed to help free them from their reflective prison and give you a reward for your assistance.

'''Congratulations! Quest Complete!'''

==Rewards==
* 1x [[Ulv's longbow]] and the subsequent recipe

Mount:
'''Mount''' is a mechanic that was introduced with the release of [[Fellhollow]]. It was highly requested by players who wanted a faster means to travel through [[Ashenfall]]. 
==Mechanics==
When on a mount, players can travel through terrain, and their stamina lasts longer as well. There are two base mount versions: the '''terrorbird''' and '''magic carpet'''. If the player is attacked, dealt damage, or is building up [[Wither]], the mount will vanish.

=== Types of Mounts ===
The list below are of the different types of mounts and their functions:
* '''Terrorbirds''': Terrorbird mounts are unlocked upon completing [[The Wild Hunt]]. Terrorbirds give +200 carry weight, making them good for travelling when gathering supplies.
* '''Magic carpets''': Magic carpets are unlocked upon completing the first section of [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]]. They do not give bonus weight, but do make traversing through [[Umbral Sands]] easier, and are much faster in the desert compared to other mounts. They are also lighter, taking less fall damage and allowing higher jumps.

'''Player-versus-player''' combat, or '''PvP''', can be enabled for a [[Worlds|world]] when creating or editing one. When the option is enabled, players can fight each other, rather than just other [[monster]]s. 

==Creating a world==
<gallery mode="packed" widths="100" heights="100">
PVP Enabled Icon.png|PvP enabled
PVP Disabled Icon.png|PvP disabled
</gallery>
When creating a world, world owners have the option to turn on Friendly fire, enabling PvP for the world. The world owner can change this setting at any time whilst hosting the world. World owners must make sure to click on "Edit World" after making the PvP adjustment.

==Mechanics==
Players can attack each other whilst in [[Ashenfall]], [[vault]]s, or other instances (such as the boss fight with [[Velgar]]) through [[Attack|melee]], [[ranged]], and [[magic]]. If a player kills another player, the player who dealt the kill can access the player's [[gravestone]] and get their items. If a player dies and the world owner closes the world, the player who died will '''not''' be able to retrieve their items.

[[File:Ranged.png|left|width=70x70]]
'''Ranged''' is one of the [[skills]] in ''Runescape: Dragonwilds,'' is one of the three combat styles, and was released in 0.9. Fighting [[monsters]] using ranged combat levels a player's Ranged to gain various bonuses that enhance their effectiveness with the skill.

Players use [[Ranged weapons]] in combat to earn Ranged experience. The higher the tier of the weapons and ammo used, the higher the base damage and, thus, the more experience earned.

In addition, players can gain experience from [[Skill Tome - Ranged|Ranged Skill Tomes]] and special reward tomes like the [[Tome of the Dragon Slayer]].

==Equipment==
===Weapons===
[[Ranged Weapons]] can be divided into three major classifications:

* [[Longbow|'''Longbows''']] require [[arrows]] and must be drawn while aiming, providing players with an advantage in long-range combat.  Fully drawing the bow takes more time than shortbows but provides higher base damage and an additional damage bonus.  Attacking without aiming will instead use a [[melee]]-based attack to push away close enemies.
* '''[[Shortbows]]''' require [[arrows]] and can be drawn without aiming, allowing players to release arrows in close combat quickly.  Shortbows have lower base damage than their longbow counterparts but have an increased firing rate.
* '''[[Crossbows]]''' require [[bolts]], are optimal at short distances, and fire quicker than shortbows.  They are also a one-handed ranged weapon, allowing players to utilise [[shields]] to [[parry]].

===Ammunition===
* '''[[Arrows]]''' are used with [[bows]] and can be modified to apply [[Debuffs]].
** [[Weapon barbs]] applies [[Bleed]].
** [[Weapon poison]] applies [[Poison]].
** [[Fire oil]] applies [[Burning|Burn]].

* '''[[Bolts]]''' are used with crossbows and can be enchanted with [[gems]] using [[Magic]] for added effects.
** [[Enchanted bronze bolts]] use [[opal]]s and provide a chance to apply a knockdown effect.
** [[Enchanted blurite bolts]] use [[jade]]s and provide a chance to apply an area-of-effect damage.
** [[Enchanted iron bolts]] use [[jade]]s and provide a chance to apply a knockdown effect.
** [[Enchanted steel bolts]] use [[red topaz]] and provide a chance to recover [[health]].
** [[Enchanted mithril bolts]] use [[sapphire]] and provide a chance to [[poison]] all nearby enemies.

===Armour===
[[Ranged armour]] provides a base defensive stat but also provides a stacking passive bonus, the more of the same combat type (i.e., melee, ranged, mage) you equip. Players can mix and match within that type. For example, a player wearing a [[ranger hat]] (ranged), [[green dragonhide body]] (ranged), and [[white platelegs]] (melee) will get the second tier of ranged set bonuses and the first tier of melee set bonuses. The ranged armour set bonuses are:

* 1/3 +40% [[stealth]] speed
* 2/3 -33% ranged attack stamina cost
* 3/3 +25% [[weak point]] damage

==Boosts==
Players can eat [[food]] or equip [[trinkets]] to increase Ranged experience received or damage dealt.

Unlike most other [[skills]] however, there are no '''Ranged''' potions, whether to increase experience or damage.

* [[Sweet veg ball]] - Grants a 10% XP boost for 5 minutes (300 seconds)
* [[Wild pie]] - Grants a 10% XP boost for 10 minutes (600 seconds)
* [[Inspiring amulet of Ranged]] - Provides a 5% XP boost for Ranged while worn
* [[Amulet of accuracy]] - Increases critical damage by 12.5% while worn
* [[Unholy Symbol|Unholy symbol]] - Increases all damage by 15% while lowering maximum HP by 15 points.
* [[Amulet of glory]] - Increases critical damage to all combat style

==Experience mechanics==
Players who deal regular damage will receive <math>0.25 \times damage\ dealt</math> experience depending on the maximum health of the enemy. Players who deal critical damage will receive <math>0.5 \times damage\ dealt</math> experience, depending on the maximum health of the enemy.  For example, if a player deals 88 regular damage to a [[chicken]], the player will only receive 5 Ranged experience, since the maximum health of the chicken is 20 hitpoints (20 hitpoints x .25 experience factor = 5 experience).

{{external|os|rs|rsc=Weapon}}
[[File:Weapon Rack (Weapons).png|right|frameless|230px]]
'''Weapons''' are items that can be used to deal [[Health|damage]] to enemies or to other players in a [[Player-versus-player|PvP]]-enabled server. Their damage types are represented by the RuneScape combat triangle, and can come in 3 types - [[Attack|Melee]], [[ranged]], and [[magic]]. They are crafted via various furniture such as the [[crafting table]], [[blacksmith's bench]], [[fletching bench]], [[mystic forge]]. They can be repaired there as well if their [[durability]] drops or they break. The various foes in the world are weak to and resist certain types of attacks, so a varied arsenal is paramount for ease of exploration in [[Ashenfall]]. 

Various monsters and chests within the world have a chance to contain recipes for new weapons, which can be read and then crafted at their respective workshop. 

* See [[stamina]] for a breakdown of the stamina costs for using each weapon, or [[combat]] for a complete list of the damage per second for each weapon and style, enemy weaknesses, etc.

==Melee Weapons==
Melee weapons are currently split into two categories: one-handed and two-handed weapons.

Attack Combos shown include the bonus attacks awarded by [[Weapon Expertise]], unlocked at 16 [[Attack]].

* 1-handed and 2-handed weapons can utilise the block mechanic without a shield.

==Ranged Weapons==
Ranged weapons are currently split into three categories: shortbows, longbows, and crossbows.

* Shortbows can be effectively used at both close and moderate ranges, but do less damage than their counterparts. 
* Longbows are very high-damage, long-range weapons, but difficult to use at close range. 
* Crossbows are one-handed and do moderate damage, but are only effective at relatively short range. 

===Shortbows===
Shortbows can either be drawn, or quick-fired with a reduction in range and damage. They have the lowest per-shot damage of the ranged weapons and moderate range, but the fastest fire-rate when quick-firing.

===Battlestaves===

Battlestaves can expend a large amount of magical energy at once through a secondary attack, based on the rune used. This consumes 5 runes per cast.
** Air: Stuns and knocks back enemies. Increases damage and stun based on charge time.
** Fire: Breathe fire in a cone in front of you. Increases duration, not damage, of the cone based on charge time at 2-5 ticks of damage.
** Water: Conjures a bubble of magic water that damages all enemies around the player when released. It then creates a field of magic water that heals allies standing on it over time. Increases both the first damage and the duration and size of the field based on charge.

== Walkthrough ==

=== Part I: The Gate Opens ===
To start this quest, players must have completed [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]]. After that, head back into the Fractured Plains and head north-west of Velgar's Rise. You will soon come across a Dragon Gate that will take you into the Scorned Wilderness. Interact with the gate and it will tell you that the blood of the four seal the gate. It will then tell you that the lord of the skies has fallen, [[Xikotal]] slain by [[Kuldra]], Velgar's cruelty no longer infects the earth, Imaru finally rests in peace, and Fuzan's flames have been extinguished. Choose the option to journey into the Scorned Wilderness.

'''Note:''' ''This will play the narrative trailer for the [[Scorned Wilderness]].''

Once you pass through the gate, the journey begins. Speak to [[Commander Zilyana|Zilyana]] in [[Scorned Wilderness#Rasthin's Rest|Rasthin's Rest]]. She explains that she was sent there by [[Saradomin]] to deal with the threat, but requires your aid, as getting closer to Kuldra's lair weakens her. Zilyiana mentions that the location you are in makes a perfect base, it is advised that you build a new base here so that you can return after using a checkpoint, rest, craft and so on. After you have set up a base here, speak to Zilyana to continue to the first location.

Speak to Zilyana, and start the raid, you will be transported to [[Scorned Wilderness#Dragontail Vines|Dragontail Vines]]. 

'''Note:''' ''For a strategy guide, see [[Scorned Wilderness]]. You'll need to clear the raid in order to complete the quest.''

=== Part II: Death of a Queen ===
After defeating Kuldra, Zilyana will transport you back to Rasthin's Rest, where she will inform you that due to the veil, their deeds will go unnoticed for now. You are rewarded for your help.

'''''Congratulations! Quest Complete!'''''

**Each time you complete a run, you will be forced to start again in '''Dragontail Vines'''.
*[[Lougrim's Staff]]

==== Additional rewards/activities ====
After the quest, players can take Lougrim's Staff into Umbral Sands and speak to [[Ancamairon - Alcarrid Elder]] to receive the [[Lougrim Memorial Shrine]] furniture reward.

[[File:Rune Altar Menu.png|right|320px|Rune Altar Menu]]
The [[rune altar]] is a crafting table used to craft [[runes]] using [[rune essence]]. Its menu displays options to select which [[rune]] you want to craft, a slider for how many you want to craft (from 1 to 50), and has two different methods to do so—Attune and Auto Craft:
* Attuning is a two-step process involving [[Runecrafting#Attunement|Attunement]] and [[Runecrafting#Infusion|Infusion]] and can award the maximum available XP and [[rune essence]] to [[runes]] ratio of 1:10.
* [[Runecrafting#Auto Crafting|Auto Crafting]] instantly crafts [[runes]] but only awards 25% of the XP and requires [[Air Efficiency|Efficiency]] upgrades to get the 1:10 ratio.

===Attunement===
[[File:Low Attunement.png|right|320px|Low Attunement]]
[[File:Medium Attunement.png|right|320px|Medium Attunement]]
[[File:High Attunement.png|right|320px|High Attunement]]
''Find an attunement frequency to infuse the runes with magical energy. Higher attunement levels grant additional bonus runes.''

The [[Runecrafting#Attunement|attunement phase]] brings up the player's chosen rune with frequencies surrounding it with a pointer facing outwards. By moving the pointer around the [[rune]], it will resonate with low, medium, and high frequencies. By locking in the resonance (default LMB on MnK), It will display the [[Runecrafting#Attunement|attunement]] strength (weak, moderate, or strong), the number of bonus runes to expect (33%, 66%, or 100% more), and the difficulty (easy, normal, or hard).

At lower Runecrafting levels, this phase lasts a short time, and the frequencies may shift before the player can find and lock in the one they want. However, there's nothing lost by failing to lock in a resonance—In fact, hitting the escape key will back out of the [[Runecrafting#Attunement|Attunement Phase]] with nothing lost except time. With experience (both numerical and literal), finding the desired frequency can be achieved quickly. Every level will increase the phase by 0.6% up to a maximum of 58.8%. 

===Infusion===
[[File:Failed Infusion.png|right|320px|Failed Infusion]]
[[File:Perfect Infusion.png|right|320px|Perfect Infusion]]
''As the attuned rune fills with power, mend its cracks to contain the magic within and safeguard you bonus runes.''

The [[Runecrafting#Infusion|Infusion Phase]] then rotates the pointer inwards. Cracks will begin to appear on the rune which the player will need to seal. Attempting to seal a crack will halt the pointer, so the player will need to be sure to only click on cracks. The pointer moves slower with short mouse movements but will move faster to keep up with larger movements, and will even flip across the [[rune]] if needed. It is good practice to overshoot a crack with the mouse but then seal the crack as soon as the pointer reaches it.

At lower Runecrafting levels, this phase can last a long time, and it can become difficult to keep up with how many cracks appear. There will be a maximum of five cracks at once, and a few seconds of that will drain the bonus runes you would have received to slightly less than what you would have gotten by [[Runecrafting#Auto Crafting|auto crafting]]. However, even a failed infusion will award more XP than [[Runecrafting#Auto Crafting|auto crafting]]. Levels 17, 48, and 78 unlock [[Lesser Infusion Duration|Infusion Duration reductions]], such that there's only enough time for 5 cracks to even appear starting at level 78.

There is a delay between when a crack first appears and when it begins draining bonus runes, and by sealing all of the cracks before they begin draining, it is possible to achieve a '''Perfect Infusion'''. Again, with practice and experience, this becomes easier and more reliable to perform. Due to this, although Low and Medium [[Runecrafting#Attunement|Attunement]] is a good introduction to attuning, the player should prioritize '''High Attunements and Perfect Infusions''' in order to maximize their runes and experience received.

===Auto Craft===
As stated before, [[Runecrafting#Auto Crafting|Auto Crafting]] instantly crafts [[runes]] but only awards 25% of the XP and requires [[Air Efficiency|Efficiency]] upgrades to get the 1:10 ratio—it otherwise only provides a ratio of 1:5.

Although it is an option to quickly create [[runes]] without performing the minigame, the high level requirements for some of the [[runes]] [[Law Efficiency|Efficiency Upgrades]], and the significantly hampered experience, it is not recommended to [[Runecrafting#Auto Crafting|auto craft]], at the very least not until level 99.

==Anima Vents==
{{Map|Air Anima Vent,Astral Anima Vent,Earth Anima Vent,Fire Anima Vent,Law Anima Vent,Nature Anima Vent,Water Anima Vent}}
[[Anima vent]]s can be found throughout [[Ashenfall]], and produce sounds and runes specific to their type. The player can siphon [[runes]] from them using [[rune essence]] at any level, making them a source of runes that the player may not yet be able to craft. Like other resource nodes, they respawn after 3 in-game days.

Each normal node will turn 10 [[rune essence]] into 100 [[runes]] and 40 XP, or 70 XP with 45% XP Boosts. With [[Lesser Anima Siphoning]] at level 46, the runes will increase to 120, a ratio of 1:12, and with [[Greater Anima Siphoning]] it will further increase to 150 per 10 [[rune essence]], or a ratio of 1:15.

[[Anima vent]]s have a chance to be '''concentrated''', which means they will have triple the available runes as long as they player has triple the available essence. With the previous two abilities, that means that the player can get up to 450 runes and 120/210 XP for only 30 rune essence from a '''concentrated''' vent with [[Greater Anima Siphoning]]. Also with [[Greater Elemental Spirits]] at level 64, the [[Summon Elemental Spirits]] spell from level 19 will indicate any '''concentrated''' vents.

In addition, starting at level 34, there is a 1/5 chance while siphoning for a [[Pure Essence]] rock to appear, which will float in the air and move quickly. It disappears after a short time, but by hitting it with a [[Magic|combat spell]], [[Ranged|arrow, or bolt]], it will provide 700 XP and 20-30 additional runes that match the vent as well as 20-30 additional nature and law runes.

And finally, with [[Runes to Rune Essence]] at level 61 and especially with [[Runes to Rune Essence|Runes to Rune Essence Upgrade]] at level 81 giving back 40% and 60% of the [[rune essence]], the player can interact with every [[anima vent]] they come across and almost entirely refund the [[rune essence]] consumed, gaining free siphon XP as well as a chance for a [[Pure Essence]] rock. Even if they don't have any [[rune essence]] on hand, they can generate some with the spell using [[runes]] that don't weigh anything and from the rune Pouch which is separate from the inventory.

'''Seeking Salvation''' is a secondary [[Quests|quest]] where players help [[Doric]] search for more valuable relics.

==Overview==
{{Quest details
|desc = Find the statues to gain entrance to the vault and uncover the secrets that lie within.
|enemies = 
* [[Zombie]]s (Can appear outside of the vault)
* [[Skeleton]]s
* [[Dragon wolf|Dragon wolves]]
* [[Vault archon]]
* [[Vault guardian hulk]]
* [[Vault overlord]]
|item_req = 
* 5 [[air rune]]s to cast [[Windstep]] or resources to build [[foundations]] and [[stairs]] to certain statues
* [[Iron pickaxe]] or better
* [[Torch]] or the spell [[Fire Spirit]] (if too dark or in a cave)
|qtype = secondary
|rec =
* Good [[armor]] and [[weapons]]
* [[Food]] and [[water]]
|req = * Partial completion of [[Withering Heights]], to gain access to [[Fellhollow]]
|start = Speak to [[Doric]] east of the [[Lake of Lost Souls]], inside a cave.
}}

==Walkthrough==
===Starting off===
The quest can be started by talking to Doric east of the [[Lake of Lost Souls]], inside a cave ruin. He'll inform you that the vault door is sealed by magic and requires you to unlock it. To unlock it, look for four dragonkin statues; activate them to unlock the door.
# One statue is located '''outside the cave entrance''', before entering the cave.
# A statue can be found south-west of Doric, behind the giant pillar. If it is too dark, bring out your torch for better lighting.
# One is located on the top of the pillar, directly west of Doric. You will require the [[Windstep]] spell or build some [[foundation]] and/or [[stairs]].
# The final statue is located north-west of Doric; there will be some rot. Use [[Windstep]] or build some stairs at the location. There will be a cracked wall; you will need a [[Pickaxes|pickaxe]] to break it.
<gallery mode="nolines" widths="300" heights="300">
File:SeekingSalvationStatue1.png
File:SeekingSalvationStatue2.png
File:SeekingSalvationStatue3.png
File:SeekingSalvationStatue4.png
File:SeekingSalvationStatue4 2.png
</gallery>

===Skekven Kara===
Once you have located and activated all four statues, you can enter the [[Skekven Kara]] [[dragonkin vault|vault]]. Make sure to bring plenty of cooked [[food]] and drinks (such as [[clean water]] or [[infusions]]) as there are multiple enemies within. 

Inside the Skekven Kara vault, proceed in the entry room to the central staircase. At the second highest level of the stairs, an opening in the wall south of the staircase can be reached by using Windstep. In this cavern, interact with the dragonkin statue to learn the secrets, which Doric can translate.

==Rewards==
* 1 [[salve crystal]]
** This also unlocks the permanent option to purchase more crystals from [[Death (Grim Reaper)|Death's Exchange]] for 25 [[soul fragment]]s each.
* The recipe to craft a [[salve amulet]]

The '''Settings''' screen can be found whilst starting the ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' client. Below are features that players can adjust to enhance their gameplay:

==Gameplay==
===Gameplay===
====Hide Chat====
Players have the option to hide the chat overlay completely. To do so, they must confirm their choice by clicking on the box on the right. This option is disabled by default.

====Gravestone Protection====
Players can choose to prevent other players from accessing their gravestone. This option is disabled by default.

====Screen Shake====
Players can choose to disable or enable screen shake during combat. This option is enabled by default.

===Camera===
====Sensitivity X====
This option controls the generic mouse sensitivity along the x-axis across the game. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. Sensitivity X is set to five by default.

====Sensitivity Y====
This option controls the generic mouse sensitivity along the y-axis across the game. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. Sensitivity Y is set to five by default.

====ADS Sensitivity X====
This option controls the mouse sensitivity when aiming down sight (ADS) along the x-axis. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. ADS Sensitivity X is set to five by default.

====ADS Sensitivity Y====
This option controls the mouse sensitivity when aiming down sight (ADS) along the y-axis. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. ADS Sensitivity Y is set to five by default.

====Invert X / Horizontal====
This option can invert the horizontal axis of the mouse or joystick. Players can confirm their choice by clicking on the box on the right.

====Invert Y / Vertical====
This option can invert the vertical axis of the mouse or joystick. Players can confirm their choice by clicking on the box on the right.

===Controls===
====Press To Sprint====
Players can press the Sprint key to toggle sprinting on and off, rather than holding it.

==Video==
===Quality===

====Auto Detect (Quality)====
Players who click the '''APPLY''' button will automatically apply the best video quality for their computer configuration.

====Auto Detect (Performance)====
Players who click the '''APPLY''' button will automatically apply the best video performance for their computer configuration.

====Quality====
Players have five options that can drastically change the level of graphics in the game up to the level they select:

* Auto - Very low (default)
* Low
* Medium
* High
* Very high
** Choosing this option will enable Nanite.
* Epic
** Choosing this opition will enable Nanite.

====Upscaling Mode====
Upscaling mode is an algorithm used to improve visual fidelity. Players can choose to adjust this by clicking on the side buttons to change to:

* TSR (Balanced) - This option is set by default. This contains a good balance of image quality and performance, often a solid all-around choice.
* DLSS (Best) - Renders the game at a lower resolution than the target display resolution.
* FSR (Fast) - Prioritises performance, may have a softer image quality.
* NIS (Fastest) - Heavily prioritises performance, can look sharper, but might have more artefacts.
* Off - Disables any upscaling.

====Upscaling Quality====
Upscaling quality is how the game changes visual fidelity whilst moving around in-game. The options below depend on the setting chosen above:

* TSR (Balanced)
** Quality (default option)
** Ultra Quality
** Performance
** Balanced

* Off

* DX12 (default)

====Display Mode====
Players have several options that display the game on their screen.

* Full Screen Windowed (default)
* Full Screen
* Windowed - This will allow players to change the Resolution setting between 1,280x720 and any higher resolutions, depending on the player's graphics card.

====Frame Rate Limit====
Players can change the frames per second (FPS) to several thresholds:

* Dynamic (default)
* 30 frames per second
* 60 frames per second
* 90 frames per second
* 120 frames per second
* 140 frames per second

====Brightness====
[[File:Brightness calibration interface.png|thumb|right|The brightness calibration with the left ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' logo barely visible.]]

====Sharpness====
Players can adjust the sharpness from 10 (default) to 100, only if the Upscaling Mode option is set to FSR (Fast) or NIS (Fastest). 

====Depth of Field====
Players can adjust the depth of field in the game; this is set to 100 by default.

====Bloom====
Players can adjust the bloom that controls the hazy glow around light sources; this is set to 100 by default.

====Frame Generation====
Players can turn on Frame Generation only if the Upscaling Mode option is set to FSR (Fast). Depending on the player's graphics card, this may improve the image quality.

====VSync====
Players can turn on Vertical Synchronisation (VSync) to eliminate screen tearing.

===Advanced===
====GPU Crash Debugging====
Players can automatically report GPU Crash Debugging if the Steam client crashes. Note that enabling this feature has a small performance cost.

==Audio==
Players can adjust the Master, Music, SFX, and Dialogue volume. Note that all these options are set to 100 by default.

==Accessibility==

===Language===
Players set their language from its default setting, English (United Kingdom), to Spanish, French, Italian, or German.

===Font Size===
Players can set their font size from its default setting, Normal, to Large or Small.

===Enable Profanity Filtering===
Players can enable or disable the profanity filter, applying to in-game chat and players' signs. This can optionally apply to usernames and server names.

===Filter Usernames===
Players can check this box to apply the profanity filter (if set to '''enabled''') to usernames. Note that usernames will not be filtered in the server users list, so players can copy the usernames for reporting purposes. This option is set to '''disabled''' by default.

===Strong profanities===
This option determines the strength of the profanity filter if Enable Profanity Filtering is set to '''enabled'''. This option is set to '''Always''' by default.

* '''Always''' - will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of a word. For example, if "cat" is in a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s<nowiki>***</nowiki>tter" and "catfish" is filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>fish".

* '''Filter if full word" - will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For example, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>". 

* '''Ignore''' - will ignore the strong profanity filter list.

===Mild profanities===
This option determines the strength of the profanity filter if Enable Profanity Filtering is set to '''enabled'''. This option is set to '''Filter if full word''' by default.

* '''Always''' - will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of a word. For example, if "cat" is in a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s<nowiki>***</nowiki>tter" and "catfish" is filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>fish".

* '''Filter if full word" - will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For example, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>". 

* '''Ignore''' - will ignore the strong profanity filter list.

===Also filter German===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the German profanity list.

===Also filter Spanish===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Spanish (Castilian) profanity list.

===Also filter Spanish (Latin America)===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Spanish (Latin America) profanity list.

===Also filter French===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the French profanity list.

===Also filter Italian===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Italian profanity list.

===Also filter Portuguese (Brazil)===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Portuguese (PT-BR) profanity list.
